The examples share these three orders. Stable string IDs make idempotency and tenant routing explicit; prices use Decimal128, quantities use BSON int, and dates are UTC BSON dates.[35][37][54] const shop = db.getSiblingDB("shop"); if (shop.getCollectionInfos({name: "orders"}).length) { throw new Error("orders already exists: inspect it; do not reset it"); } shop.createCollection("orders", { validator: {$jsonSchema: { bsonType: "object", required: ["_id", "tenantId", "customerId", "placedAt", "status", "total", "lines"], properties: { _id: {bsonType: "string"}, tenantId: {bsonType: "string"}, customerId: {bsonType: "string"}, placedAt: {bsonType: "date"}, status: {enum: ["new", "paid", "cancelled"]}, total: {bsonType: "decimal", minimum: Decimal128("0")}, lines: {bsonType: "array", minItems: 1, maxItems: 100, items: {bsonType: "object", required: ["sku", "qty", "unitPrice"], properties: { sku: {bsonType: "string"}, qty: {bsonType: "int", minimum: 1}, unitPrice: {bsonType: "decimal", minimum: Decimal128("0")} }}} } }}, validationLevel: "strict", validationAction: "error" }); shop.orders.insertMany([ {_id: "o1001", tenantId: "t1", customerId: "c1", placedAt: ISODate("2026-09-01T09:00:00Z"), status: "new", total: Decimal128("5.00"), lines: [{sku: "pencil", qty: Int32(2), unitPrice: Decimal128("2.50")}]}, {_id: "o1002", tenantId: "t1", customerId: "c2", placedAt: ISODate("2026-09-02T09:00:00Z"), status: "paid", total: Decimal128("9.00"), lines: [{sku: "notebook", qty: Int32(1), unitPrice: Decimal128("9.00")}]}, {_id: "o1003", tenantId: "t2", customerId: "c3", placedAt: ISODate("2026-09-03T09:00:00Z"), status: "new", total: Decimal128("2.50"), lines: [{sku: "pencil", qty: Int32(1), unitPrice: Decimal128("2.50")}]} ]); shop.orders.createIndex({tenantId: 1, placedAt: -1}, {name: "tenant_recent"}); shop.orders.countDocuments({}); shop.orders.find({_id: "o1001"}).toArray(); Acceptance: the three IDs exist once, values retain their BSON types, and tenant_recent exists. A document with total: "5.00" should be rejected by validation; do not weaken the validator to import a string accidentally. Duplicate-key errors on rerun are useful evidence that the stable IDs already exist, not a reason to clear the database. If an ordered insert fails midway, inspect which IDs landed before retrying.[37][54] const shop = db.getSiblingDB("shop"); shop.orders.find({tenantId: "t1", status: "new"}, {_id: 1, total: 1}) .sort({placedAt: -1}).limit(10); shop.orders.updateOne( {_id: "o1001", tenantId: "t1", status: "new"}, {$set: {status: "paid"}} ); shop.createView("paid_orders", "orders", [ {$match: {status: "paid"}}, {$project: {_id: 1, tenantId: 1, total: 1}} ]); shop.paid_orders.find().limit(10); updateOne changes only specified fields with $set; replaceOne replaces the document body and can remove omitted fields. Include the tenant and old status to avoid an unintended transition. Ordinary views are read-only pipelines over source data; their underlying indexes determine performance.[80] Use collMod for validator changes. Inspect and save the entire current validator first; supplying a new validator replaces it, not merges it. For a staged rollout, make old data conform, enable strict/error validation, and test rejected and accepted writes. validationAction: "warn" accepts invalid data and is not a final integrity control.[37][55] shop.getCollectionInfos({name: "orders"}); shop.runCommand({collMod: "orders", validationLevel: "strict", validationAction: "error"}); MongoDB does not supply SQL foreign keys, SQL stored procedures/triggers, sequences or per-session temporary tables as interchangeable features. Enforce cross-document references and sequencing in application design; change streams are asynchronous notifications, not a synchronous constraint trigger. Do not use server-side JavaScript as a stored-procedure replacement: relevant server-side JavaScript features are deprecated in 8.0.[29][35] For deletion, preview the exact predicate and count, obtain approval and retain a backup. deleteMany({}), collection drop() and database dropDatabase() are destructive, not “reset settings.” A safer fixture cleanup uses the explicit known IDs only in a disposable database, after confirming no dependent exercise needs them; even that has no automatic undo.[54] Authenticate as useradmin on admin to administer users. A user created in shop authenticates against shop even when granted privileges elsewhere. title: Users, roles and authentication databases
context: Databases · Work with objects and access · MongoDB · Objects, users and administration
text: Authenticate as useradmin on admin to administer users. A user created in shop authenticates against shop even when granted privileges elsewhere. The same username in different authentication databases denotes different identities.[99] use shop db.createRole({ role: "orderWriter", privileges: [{resource: {db: "shop", collection: "orders"}, actions: ["find", "insert", "update"]}], roles: [] }); db.createUser({user: "shopapp", pwd: passwordPrompt(), roles: [{role: "orderWriter", db: "shop"}]}); db.getUser("shopapp", {showPrivileges: true}); db.getRole("orderWriter", {showPrivileges: true}); Identity Authentication DB Privileges shopapp shop Find/insert/update orders only; no delete, DDL or user management operator admin Cluster administration plus readWrite/dbAdmin on shop for exercises monitor admin clusterMonitor; add only required per-DB visibility backup admin backup; protect broad read access restore admin restore; additional reviewed privilege needed for oplog replay useradmin admin User/role administrator; escalation-capable, not app access Tenant isolation is not enforced by this collection role: the application must constrain tenant predicates, or use a stronger tenancy design. Test denied operations from a fresh shopapp session as well as permitted reads/writes.[18][85] // useradmin, context shop: credential rotation and role revocation examples db.changeUserPassword("shopapp", passwordPrompt()); db.revokeRolesFromUser("shopapp", [{role: "orderWriter", db: "shop"}]); // Restore approved access if revocation was a drill: db.grantRolesToUser("shopapp", [{role: "orderWriter", db: "shop"}]); Coordinate password rotation with application connection pools; test a new connection before retiring the previous deployment secret. For incident revocation, restrict network access and invalidate/close affected sessions as part of the response; changing credentials alone is not proof every old operation stopped. Keep a separate emergency administrator, not an undocumented bypass.[17][18]

title: Operations and sessions
context: Databases · Work with objects and access · MongoDB · Objects, users and administration
text: Read-only inspection first; clusterMonitor supplies broad visibility. $currentOp is preferred over deprecated db.currentOp() in 8.0. Match namespace/client/comment and inspect returned operation IDs; do not kill by an example ID copied from notes.[19][51] const admin = db.getSiblingDB("admin"); admin.aggregate([ {$currentOp: {allUsers: true, idleConnections: false}}, {$match: {active: true, ns: "shop.orders", secs_running: {$gte: 5}}}, {$project: {opid: 1, ns: 1, secs_running: 1, client: 1, command: 1, waitingForLock: 1, lsid: 1}} ]).toArray(); Prefer application cancellation and maxTimeMS on bounded reads. db.killOp(observedOpId) asks the server to interrupt a particular operation; it is not a Linux process kill. Run only against the confirmed target, with killop privileges when killing another user’s work. In a sharded cluster use the documented router-aware operation identifier/path; do not strip shard information from an ID.[51][53] killSessions takes observed session identifiers and can terminate related work/cursors/transactions. It is broader than one operation and distinct from ending your own shell session with endSession(). Prepared transactions are an exception: killSessions ignores their sessions rather than undoing a prepared distributed transaction.[17] Review ownership, topology and privileges first. After cancellation, inspect operations and application outcome; a write already committed is not undone.[17][53]

title: Runtime settings versus startup configuration
context: Databases · Work with objects and access · MongoDB · Objects, users and administration
text: const admin = db.getSiblingDB("admin"); const prior = admin.runCommand({getParameter: 1, logLevel: 1}); if (prior.ok !== 1) throw new Error("could not capture prior logLevel"); printjson(prior); // Also save securely outside this session. try { admin.runCommand({setParameter: 1, logLevel: 1}); // Capture a short, supervised diagnostic window here. } finally { admin.runCommand({setParameter: 1, logLevel: prior.logLevel}); } admin.runCommand({getParameter: 1, logLevel: 1}); Use an account authorized for setParameter; restore and verify the observed prior value rather than assuming zero. If the shell disconnects, reconnect and restore the externally saved value. Verbose logging adds overhead and can expose data. setParameter is node-scoped/runtime for supported parameters, not a broadcast to all members and not persistence through restart. Put an approved persistent value in YAML under its documented setting and schedule a restart; daemon-reload does not reload MongoDB YAML.[6][16]

title: Architecture, editions and tools
context: Databases · Understand the moving parts · MongoDB
text: These notes use self-managed MongoDB Community 8.0, WiredTiger, RHEL 9 x86_64, SELinux enforcing and systemd, using MongoDB vendor RPMs (not Red Hat AppStream). The concrete package baseline is 8.0.29; shell mongosh 2.10.0; Database Tools 100.17.0. Tools and shell have their own release numbers: neither is “MongoDB Tools 8.0.” Examples below are independent snippets, not one script to paste end-to-end. Use a fresh shell or a local block when repeating snippets that declare const bindings. These are pinned documentation targets, not a promise that a mutable repository still retains every package. Check package availability before changing a host.[4][5][48] 8.0 is a major release supported for on-premises use. The published Server lifecycle lists October 31, 2029 as 8.0 end-of-life under Enterprise Advanced; that date is not an entitlement to commercial support for a Community installation. RHEL 9 x86_64 is explicitly in the Community 8.0 installation matrix. Review advisories and supported OS/kernel combinations before adopting any pinned patch.[4][104][50] Choice What it supplies What not to assume Community Self-managed server, replication, sharding, transactions, authorization, TLS No Enterprise audit or encrypted storage engine Enterprise Advanced Commercial distribution and subscription features Installation alone does not configure backup, auditing or key custody Atlas Managed service, tier-dependent backup/security features Not the procedure or free substitute used here Community SSPL Source available under Server Side Public License Not an OSI-approved open-source license; offering it as a service requires license review Feature and license boundaries matter more than the download label. Community logs/profiling are not a security audit trail. Community can use host/volume encryption, but it has no security.enableEncryption equivalent to Enterprise’s encrypted storage engine.[11][15][47] Program Runs where Job mongod Each data-bearing host Stores documents/indexes; runs replication and query execution mongos Router host(s) Routes requests to shards; no application dbPath mongosh Administrator workstation or DB host JavaScript/BSON shell; separately packaged Driver Application Authentication, server discovery, pooling, read preference, retries mongodump / mongorestore Backup worker BSON logical dump/restore, metadata and index definitions mongoexport / mongoimport Migration worker JSON/CSV interchange; not a complete backup mongostat / mongotop Monitor Server activity and collection time samples bsondump Operator workstation Inspect BSON offline; can expose sensitive contents The vendor RPM repository and Red Hat OS repositories have separate provenance/support responsibilities. mongodb-org-server, mongodb-org-mongos, mongodb-mongosh and mongodb-database-tools have different contents; a tarball does not create the package’s service user/configuration.[105][104] application -> driver pool -> TLS handshake -> authentication -> authorization per operation standalone: mongod -> plan/execution -> WiredTiger replica set: driver discovers rs0 -> primary (writes) -> eligible member (reads) sharded: driver -> mongos -> config metadata/routing cache -> shard replica-set primary/eligible reader -> merge results -> client Authentication establishes the user and authentication database; authorization checks roles against the target database/collection. TLS protects and authenticates the transport peer, not the user’s object privileges. A session is not a new authenticated socket for every operation: drivers pool connections and carry session identifiers across operations.[18][40][95] The server matches a query shape to candidate access plans. Index scans may still fetch full documents; a collection scan is not automatically a bug on a tiny collection. explain distinguishes planning from measured execution, while the profiler records completed work. See measure an access path.[24] A replica set keeps copies of the same dataset and elects a primary. Sharding partitions data across replica sets; mongos uses the shard key and routing metadata to target requests. Adding secondaries does not distribute writes to one unsharded collection. Adding shards does not rescue a poor shard key.[30][32][34] RPM defaults for this target are established by the versioned package specification, configuration and unit, not generic installation-page defaults:[100][101][102] /usr/bin/ mongod, mongos; separately packaged clients /etc/mongod.conf YAML startup configuration /usr/lib/systemd/system/mongod.service vendor unit /etc/sysconfig/mongod optional unit environment overrides /run/mongodb/ vendor unit runtime directory /var/log/mongodb/mongod.log diagnostic log /var/lib/mongo/ storage.dbPath WiredTiger* engine metadata and supporting files _mdb_catalog.wt catalog metadata (implementation detail) collection-*.wt collection storage index-*.wt index storage WiredTigerHS.wt history store journal/ WiredTiger write-ahead journal diagnostic.data/ diagnostic samples mongod.lock process/storage locking information Names are illustrative, not an API or recovery recipe. Do not rename, remove or mix .wt files. A secondary index is a separate structure; ordinary _id indexing does not mean every collection is physically clustered like InnoDB. Back up the coherent instance, not selected engine files.[10][21] Logical database Purpose admin Administrative commands and users commonly authenticated against admin local Node-local replication data, including replica configuration/oplog; not ordinary replicated app data config Internal metadata, especially sharded cluster placement; never hand-edit routing records shop Dataset used throughout these notes: orders, later customers and inventory The RPM service runs as mongod:mongod, not a login/application user. Give the service user exclusive write access to its data/log directories. Separate databases inside one mongod still share storage, cache, CPU and failure domain. Use isolated instances when independent process/configuration boundaries are required; use separate hosts for real failure-domain separation.[6][31] The service’s ExecStart determines which config file is read. Explicit command-line values override corresponding YAML values (for example --bind_ip overrides net.bindIp).[86][89] Inspect the unit and parsed options rather than trusting the file’s name. Most startup configuration edits need a restart; setParameter changes only documented dynamic parameters and is not a persistent settings file.[6][16] // mongosh; clusterMonitor or another role allowing these inspections const admin = db.getSiblingDB("admin"); admin.runCommand({getCmdLineOpts: 1}); admin.runCommand({buildInfo: 1}); admin.runCommand({hello: 1}); // FCV is inspected on a mongod, not on mongos: if (admin.runCommand({hello: 1}).msg !== "isdbgrid") { admin.runCommand({getParameter: 1, featureCompatibilityVersion: 1}); } Record binary version, FCV, dbPath, listener, replica-set name and host list before disruptive work. hello identifies a replica-set primary/secondary or mongos (msg: "isdbgrid"); connecting to the wrong endpoint can otherwise make a valid command dangerously wrong.[6][28][34]

Back up the coherent instance, not selected engine files.[10][21] Logical database Purpose admin Administrative commands and users commonly authenticated against admin local Node-local replication data, including replica configuration/oplog; not ordinary replicated app data config Internal metadata, especially sharded cluster placement; never hand-edit routing records shop Dataset used throughout these notes: orders, later customers and inventory The RPM service runs as mongod:mongod, not a login/application user. Give the service user exclusive write access to its data/log directories. Separate databases inside one mongod still share storage, cache, CPU and failure domain. Use isolated instances when independent process/configuration boundaries are required; use separate hosts for real failure-domain separation.[6][31]

title: Configuration and identity
context: Databases · Understand the moving parts · MongoDB · Architecture, editions and tools
text: The service’s ExecStart determines which config file is read. Explicit command-line values override corresponding YAML values (for example --bind_ip overrides net.bindIp).[86][89] Inspect the unit and parsed options rather than trusting the file’s name. Most startup configuration edits need a restart; setParameter changes only documented dynamic parameters and is not a persistent settings file.[6][16] // mongosh; clusterMonitor or another role allowing these inspections const admin = db.getSiblingDB("admin"); admin.runCommand({getCmdLineOpts: 1}); admin.runCommand({buildInfo: 1}); admin.runCommand({hello: 1}); // FCV is inspected on a mongod, not on mongos: if (admin.runCommand({hello: 1}).msg !== "isdbgrid") { admin.runCommand({getParameter: 1, featureCompatibilityVersion: 1}); } Record binary version, FCV, dbPath, listener, replica-set name and host list before disruptive work. hello identifies a replica-set primary/secondary or mongos (msg: "isdbgrid"); connecting to the wrong endpoint can otherwise make a valid command dangerously wrong.[6][28][34]

title: Backup and recovery
context: Databases · Back up, then restore · MongoDB
text: A replica set copies mistakes as faithfully as good writes. Set RPO (maximum accepted lost work) and RTO (time to restore useful service), then measure them with restores. A backup job finishing is not proof of either.[21][22] Method Appropriate use Consistency/recovery boundary mongodump without oplog Small logical export during a controlled write pause With writes running, collections need not represent one instant Full replica-set dump + --oplog Consistent logical restore of one replica set Captures dump-window operations, not future continuous PITR Coherent filesystem snapshot Fast physical recovery Whole data/journal state, correct engine/version and topology required Cold whole-directory copy Planned standalone outage Clean shutdown, complete directory; copying a running directory is unsafe Atlas continuous backup / Ops Manager Managed/coordinated backup products Service/subscription-specific; not bundled Community commands JSON/CSV export Interchange Omits important metadata/types/options; not backup replacement Record source binary/FCV, Tools version, topology, times, namespaces, concerns, backup checksums, encryption/key IDs and restore instructions. Encrypt backups off-host, restrict deletion, retain independent generations, and keep decryption keys available outside the failed host. Retention deletion starts only after verifying the replacement generation and policy; never delete oplog/journal files by hand.[2][3][21] Read-heavy source operation; destructive potential on destination. Use Database Tools 100.17.0 from a trusted worker; the dump/restore flags here are present in the official 100.17.0 tagged sources.[69][70] This first route targets a standalone or a deliberately quiesced replica set’s shop database. Pause all writers and schema changes for the whole dump; document the business checkpoint. backup is the source identity; the destination uses its own restore identity.[2][3][60] umask 077 sudo install -d -o "$(id -un)" -g "$(id -gn)" -m 700 /srv/backups/mongodb mongodump --host 127.0.0.1 --port 27017 --username backup \ --authenticationDatabase admin --db shop \ --archive=/srv/backups/mongodb/shop-before-change.archive.gz --gzip Use a new filename per generation. Require a successful exit status, retain stderr/logs, checksum the completed artifact and copy it off-host before treating it as protected. Resume writes only after source state and the checkpoint are recorded. This database-only archive does not automatically provide the whole instance’s users/roles.[2] Create the isolated authenticated instance at 27018, with empty target application namespaces and the same server major/FCV as the source. The documented general restore compatibility is same major or same FCV; the conservative drill here uses the same 8.0.29 binary and recorded FCV. Do not use restore as an undocumented cross-major upgrade.[2][3] mongorestore --host 127.0.0.1 --port 27018 --username restore \ --authenticationDatabase admin \ --archive=/srv/backups/mongodb/shop-before-change.archive.gz --gzip \ --nsInclude='shop.*' --nsFrom='shop.*' --nsTo='shop_restore.*' \ --stopOnError No --drop: this route restores into a new namespace. Verify first that shop_restore is absent; otherwise choose another isolated target. If the dump contains system.profile metadata and the destination has no profiling collection, also grant the destination loader dbAdmin on shop_restore for its creation, then revoke that extra role after the drill. The ordinary restore role alone is not sufficient for this case; profile documents themselves are not restored.[60][85] A failed restore can leave partial data. Do not retry over it and assume duplicate errors are harmless; preserve logs, discard only the explicitly identified disposable target, and rerun into a clean target.[3] Tool option Scope / caution --archive=FILE, --gzip Single archive plus compression; supply matching restore options --db, --collection Limits dump scope; incompatible with full consistent oplog route --dumpDbUsersAndRoles Explicit database user/role export; security-sensitive --nsInclude Restore namespace selection; quote wildcards from the shell --nsFrom, --nsTo Namespace rewrite; not allowed with oplog replay --stopOnError Stop on write errors; does not roll back already restored documents --drop Drops collections present in backup, not unrelated destination collections --config=FILE Tools sensitive-options YAML alternative; restrict permissions If restoring admin with --drop, users are replaced and authentication can fail midway unless the required existing/backup credentials work. Never use that flag casually on an operational server. Restored view pipelines and cross-namespace references must be checked after namespace rewriting, not assumed to follow application naming changes.[2][3] Use this route for a full single replica set, not mongos or a whole sharded cluster. Confirm oplog history spans the dump, sufficient disk, stable topology and no prohibited DDL/user/role/default-concern changes during the dump. An oplog rollover or prohibited operation makes the attempt unusable; inspect the tool exit/log rather than preserving a partial dump as “success.”[2][31] The host names/CA come from the secured replica set. On the backup worker: mongodump --uri='mongodb://db1.example.net:27017,db2.example.net:27017,db3.example.net:27017/?replicaSet=rs0&authSource=admin' \ --username backup --ssl --sslCAFile=/etc/mongodb/tls/ca.pem \ --oplog --out=/srv/backups/mongodb/rs0-full-001 Do not add --db, --collection, or query filters. Ordinary dump metadata recreates indexes/views; the root oplog.bson carries captured changes. Freeze schema and privilege changes during this window even though ordinary application writes may continue. A full dump includes sensitive user/role definitions; protect it accordingly.[2] Destination-only privilege escalation for recovery. Use a fresh isolated 27018 instance, not the populated target of the preceding exercise. Bootstrap its administrator with the unique name drill_useradmin instead of useradmin, and create drill_restore with the ordinary restore role. Confirm neither name occurs in the source backup; select different names if they do. Do not create the other source-named bootstrap accounts on this destination. Authenticated as drill_useradmin, add the temporary replay role below. Oplog replay requires broader access than the ordinary restore role:[60][85] use admin db.createRole({role: "oplogReplayOnlyForDrill", privileges: [ {resource: {anyResource: true}, actions: ["anyAction"]} ], roles: []}); db.grantRolesToUser("drill_restore", [{role: "oplogReplayOnlyForDrill", db: "admin"}]); Restore the entire dump into this otherwise empty isolated deployment. Its bootstrap users must not conflict with source users carrying different credentials: establish the credential/role restoration plan before running, and never experiment against production admin.[3][60] mongorestore --host 127.0.0.1 --port 27018 --username drill_restore \ --authenticationDatabase admin --dir=/srv/backups/mongodb/rs0-full-001 \ --oplogReplay --stopOnError No namespace filter/rewrite with --oplogReplay. Retain source recovery credentials securely for post-restore administration; verify whether the restore identity/role changed, then revoke/remove the temporary replay privilege using the effective administrator. The distinct destination recovery identities above avoid name collisions, but still require a post-restore access review. Revoke the temporary role from drill_restore, remove the temporary role, and disable/remove the recovery accounts only after proving an approved source administrator can authenticate on the restored target. Do not remove your sole working administrator.[3][60] --oplogLimit is not a universal “restore to any timestamp” switch. The dump captures only its own window, not earlier consistent baselines or later writes; arbitrary truncation can produce inconsistent data. Continuous PITR needs a verifie

title: Physical snapshot and cold restore
context: Databases · Back up, then restore · MongoDB · Backup and recovery
text: A physical backup contains storage-engine state. Keep all data and journal files coherent. For online snapshots, use an atomic storage snapshot across the required volumes; if data and journal are separated, lock/suspend writes as documented. Snapshot copy-on-write space must survive until the full backup copy completes. A snapshot on the same failed disk is not offsite protection.[21] A simple self-hosted cold standalone route avoids storage-vendor snapshot syntax. Have sudo access, a write pause, a clean backup destination and a supported filesystem. Stop the source cleanly, verify termination, then copy the whole directory: sudo systemctl stop mongod sudo systemctl is-active mongod sudo install -d -o root -g root -m 700 /srv/backups/mongodb sudo mkdir -m 700 /srv/backups/mongodb/cold-001 sudo cp -a /var/lib/mongo/. /srv/backups/mongodb/cold-001/ sudo systemctl start mongod Do not proceed from is-active alone if a separate manually launched process can own the path. Record successful copy/ownership and source restart checks, then encrypt/checksum/copy the artifact off-host. Record numeric UID/GID, mount identity, SELinux local rules and policy revision alongside config/unit/TLS key identifiers (not private key contents). On an isolated recovery host, stop mongod-restore, move its disposable previous directory aside, create an empty owned /srv/mongodb/restore, and copy the full backup there. Keep the original backup read-only; start only a working copy with the matching storage options, bound to loopback at 27018.[21][22] The restore-service policy gate applies to physical restores too. Copying preserved labels/numeric owners from the source does not prove destination correctness. On the stopped disposable target only, set the restored tree to that host’s mongod:mongod, apply its persistent dbPath mapping with restorecon, and verify the mount, DAC, effective labels and confined startup. Do not recursively relabel the retained immutable backup or expose restored replica identities to production.[100][110] # Target only; the complete backup has already been copied and validated. sudo chown -R mongod:mongod /srv/mongodb/restore sudo restorecon -Rv /srv/mongodb/restore sudo ls -ldZ /srv/mongodb/restore sudo systemctl start mongod-restore sudo ps -eZ | grep mongod sudo ausearch -m AVC,USER_AVC -ts recent For a replica-set physical backup, node-local replication identity comes with the files. Do not start a restored member on the production network. To form a new set from it:[22] Work on the isolated copied directory; start it as a standalone, preserving storage/TLS/auth settings but without production replica-set membership. Authenticate using restored administrative credentials. On this isolated copy only, confirm host/path/port, then remove old node-local replication metadata: // DESTRUCTIVE: isolated restored copy only, never a live member // Requires authorized administrative access to local. db.getSiblingDB("local").dropDatabase(); Shut down cleanly. Add a new replication.replSetName, internal key and isolated host addresses; restart, initiate a single-member recovery set, then add empty secondaries for initial sync. Validate the restored data and newly built topology before cutover. Never clone the same stale membership into several running nodes and hope election makes it safe. The local removal is not a corruption repair or routine replica-member replacement. On Enterprise encrypted storage with AES256-GCM, cold-restore key rollover has additional mandatory requirements; this Community/OS-encrypted baseline does not cover that feature by pretending the same copy is sufficient.[11][22]

title: Sharded backup means coordinated backup
context: Databases · Back up, then restore · MongoDB · Backup and recovery
text: Stopping the balancer alone does not stop application writes. Exact cluster-wide consistency requires no in-flight operations and coordinated quiescence of shards and config-server metadata. Different independent per-shard dumps/snapshots can cut a cross-shard transaction or migration at different points.[26] For the documented 8.0 filesystem route, schedule an outage/window, block new writers and DDL/resharding, wait for in-flight work, and use the appropriate maintenance identities: On mongos, sh.stopBalancer(); verify sh.getBalancerState() is false and no balancing round/migration remains. Run db.getSiblingDB("admin").fsyncLock() on mongos and separately on the config-server replica-set primary. The router lock covers shard writes; config metadata must also be locked. Confirm lock results and the documented $currentOp lock diagnostics on both endpoints. Snapshot the config-server primary and every shard primary, including each node’s coherent data/journal volumes. Record one topology-wide backup manifest; do not omit the config backup. In guaranteed cleanup, issue db.getSiblingDB("admin").fsyncUnlock() on both locked endpoints, verify unlocked state, then restore the prior balancer state and admit traffic. If any snapshot/lock fails, mark the whole set incomplete, unlock what was locked and repeat from a clean window. Do not label the surviving shard files a consistent cluster backup.[26] fsyncLock disrupts writes; retain an independent operator connection and a time-bounded recovery plan. Storage-provider snapshot commands depend on the actual volume layout and are not invented here. Restoring a sharded physical backup must rebuild the matching topology/config metadata in isolation; do not apply the single-replica-set local recipe blindly to a whole cluster. Ops Manager/Atlas provide separately licensed/managed coordinated alternatives; they are options, not Community commands.[22][26][60]

title: Managed continuous backup is a separate service
context: Databases · Back up, then restore · MongoDB · Backup and recovery
text: Atlas Cloud Backup is a configured service feature, unavailable on Free clusters. Its snapshot storage uses the cloud provider; cross-region copies, retention and restoration permissions remain explicit customer decisions. A cluster existing in Atlas does not prove a recoverable backup policy exists.[81] Atlas point-in-time restore requires Continuous Cloud Backup on an eligible dedicated cluster and a timestamp within the retained restore window; scheduled snapshots alone do not establish that capability.[93][97] Select the source time and compatible destination, rehearse application cutover, and validate the restored business checkpoint. Sharded restores require topology-aware handling, not independent selection of convenient shard timestamps.[90][93] Ops Manager coordinates snapshot capture and oplog collection using deployed agents and its backup storage. It is an independently installed/operated backup product, not an additional flag on Community mongodump. Confirm deployment-version support, subscription/entitlements, agent reachability, storage capacity and recovery credentials before choosing it. Neither service removes the need to test restores or protect deletion authority.[83]

title: Restore acceptance
context: Databases · Back up, then restore · MongoDB · Backup and recovery
text: Use operator with readWrite/dbAdmin on the restored database, not just the write-oriented restore account. On 27018, grant these destination-only roles as needed via useradmin and revoke after the drill.[18][59] const restored = db.getSiblingDB("shop_restore"); restored.getCollectionInfos(); restored.orders.getIndexes(); restored.orders.countDocuments({}); restored.orders.aggregate([ {$group: {_id: "$tenantId", orders: {$sum: 1}, amount: {$sum: "$total"}}}, {$sort: {_id: 1}} ]).toArray(); restored.runCommand({validate: "orders", full: true}); For full oplog/physical restores the database is shop, not shop_restore. validate can be expensive and affect concurrency; run the full check on the isolated copy. Acceptance includes no tool errors, engine validation, expected BSON types, validators, indexes/uniqueness, views, users/roles, checkpoint-matched business totals, representative application reads/writes and measured restore time. Compare to the backup checkpoint, not a source that continued changing.[3][59] Keep the source authoritative until acceptance. A failed drill leaves the source untouched; repair backup policy rather than deleting the only known-good copy. Once a restored system accepts new writes, rollback requires reconciliation, not simply redirecting clients to an older snapshot.

title: Installation and first start
context: Databases · Get a server running · MongoDB
text: Host mutation on an authorized fresh host only. The baseline is RHEL 9 x86_64, current supported RHEL errata, systemd, SELinux Enforcing, and MongoDB Community 8.0.29 vendor RPMs. This is MongoDB’s repository, not a Red Hat AppStream package or a Red Hat support entitlement. RHEL 9 x86_64 is in MongoDB’s supported platform matrix.[104] Verify AVX-capable supported CPU, OS/kernel advisories, storage capacity and mount persistence; prefer XFS for WiredTiger. Keep RHEL kernel/glibc/OpenSSL maintained through the organization’s Red Hat repositories. Do not substitute libraries from another distribution.[62] cat /etc/redhat-release uname -m uname -r lscpu getenforce rpm -q glibc openssl-libs selinux-policy-targeted sudo dnf repolist --enabled Stop if this is not the approved RHEL 9 x86_64 platform or if existing MongoDB data/packages are present. These are fresh provisioning commands, not an in-place migration. Use sudo for OS work and a separate MongoDB identity for database work. Have authorized RHEL repositories available for dependencies. Fetch MongoDB’s 8.0 signing key, inspect its full fingerprint, and compare it with the independently approved MongoDB key record before import. RPM trust is machine-wide, unlike a per-repository keyring; gpgcheck=1 requires signed packages but is not repository-metadata signing. Do not bypass verification with --nogpgcheck.[104] sudo dnf install curl gnupg2 python3-dnf-plugin-versionlock curl -fsSLo server-8.0.asc https://pgp.mongodb.com/server-8.0.asc gpg --show-keys --with-fingerprint server-8.0.asc # STOP here until the complete fingerprint has been independently approved. sudo rpm --import server-8.0.asc Create root-owned /etc/yum.repos.d/mongodb-org-8.0.repo (0644). The RHEL 9 repository tab gives this URL; do not substitute the default tab’s RHEL 10 URL.[113] [mongodb-org-8.0] name=MongoDB Repository baseurl=https://repo.mongodb.org/yum/redhat/9/mongodb-org/8.0/x86_64/ gpgcheck=1 enabled=1 gpgkey=https://pgp.mongodb.com/server-8.0.asc The published repository metadata contains these exact NEVRAs: server/router 8.0.29-1.el9.x86_64, shell 2.10.0-1.el8.x86_64, Tools 100.17.0-1.x86_64. The shell’s el8 release tag is actually published in the RHEL 9 repository; do not invent an el9 shell build or infer its NEVRA from its shorter RPM filename. Server/router require OpenSSL 3 and glibc 2.34 symbols; DNF resolves the maintained RHEL dependencies.[106] sudo dnf --refresh --disablerepo='*' --enablerepo=mongodb-org-8.0 \ list --showduplicates mongodb-org-server mongodb-org-mongos mongodb-mongosh mongodb-database-tools sudo dnf install mongodb-org-server-8.0.29-1.el9.x86_64 \ mongodb-mongosh-2.10.0-1.el8.x86_64 mongodb-database-tools-100.17.0-1.x86_64 sudo systemctl disable --now mongod rpm -q mongodb-org-server mongodb-mongosh mongodb-database-tools sudo dnf versionlock add mongodb-org-server mongodb-mongosh mongodb-database-tools sudo dnf versionlock list Review the transaction’s repository/version/signature prompts; omit automatic yes. The server RPM enables boot start on a fresh install, so disable/stop it until bootstrap is accepted. Upgrading an active server package may try to restart it: package work is part of the maintenance window.[100] These are direct components, not a partly pinned metapackage. Install mongodb-org-mongos-8.0.29-1.el9.x86_64 only on router hosts as explained in sharding. If an exact package is unavailable, stop; review a replacement or retrieve an approved retained artifact with signature/checksum verification. Version locks select installed package NEVRAs and need scheduled security review, not permanent neglect.[112] The official policy covers standard RPM/systemd mongod installations on RHEL 9: /usr/bin/mongod, /var/lib/mongo, /var/log/mongodb, /run/mongodb, package user/unit and standard MongoDB ports. It does not cover mongos, shell/tools, arbitrary extra services or relocated paths. Changing those means a site-reviewed policy/integration, not disabling SELinux. The installation manual explicitly warns custom settings are outside the supplied policy’s standard contract.[103][104] Install the documented policy build prerequisites plus RHEL’s management/diagnostic tools. Build as an ordinary user from a reviewed immutable revision; only installation needs sudo. The revision below is the reviewed source, not permission to ignore future policy/security fixes.[103][110] sudo dnf install git make checkpolicy policycoreutils selinux-policy-devel \ policycoreutils-python-utils setools-console audit git clone https://github.com/mongodb/mongodb-selinux cd mongodb-selinux git checkout --detach 18181652362a46fd4511a56f20c4055712deb252 git rev-parse HEAD # Review source/diff and retain its revision with the deployment record. make sudo make install sudo semodule -l sudo restorecon -Rv /usr/bin/mongod /var/lib/mongo /var/log/mongodb sudo restorecon -v /usr/lib/systemd/system/mongod.service /etc/mongod.conf sudo semanage port -l | grep '^mongod_port_t' getenforce Require Enforcing, the installed mongodb policy module, and appropriate port labels before start. After start, inspect ps -eZ for mongod_t and Audit denials, not just an active unit. The policy README’s automatic-application wording is not proof the module is already installed; the versioned RPM spec does not install that policy, so the explicit build/install and readback above remain required.[100][103][108] Custom paths/ports and restore services follow instance policy integration. Keep startup blocked until that host’s confinement and file access have been checked. Package contract: the RHEL installation page currently contains conflicting generic account/directory prose; the tagged RPM specification, unit and configuration agree on the values used here. title: Package prerequisites
context: Databases · Get a server running · MongoDB · Installation and first start
text: Host mutation on an authorized fresh host only. The baseline is RHEL 9 x86_64, current supported RHEL errata, systemd, SELinux Enforcing, and MongoDB Community 8.0.29 vendor RPMs. This is MongoDB’s repository, not a Red Hat AppStream package or a Red Hat support entitlement. RHEL 9 x86_64 is in MongoDB’s supported platform matrix.[104] Verify AVX-capable supported CPU, OS/kernel advisories, storage capacity and mount persistence; prefer XFS for WiredTiger. Keep RHEL kernel/glibc/OpenSSL maintained through the organization’s Red Hat repositories. Do not substitute libraries from another distribution.[62] cat /etc/redhat-release uname -m uname -r lscpu getenforce rpm -q glibc openssl-libs selinux-policy-targeted sudo dnf repolist --enabled Stop if this is not the approved RHEL 9 x86_64 platform or if existing MongoDB data/packages are present. These are fresh provisioning commands, not an in-place migration. Use sudo for OS work and a separate MongoDB identity for database work. Have authorized RHEL repositories available for dependencies. Fetch MongoDB’s 8.0 signing key, inspect its full fingerprint, and compare it with the independently approved MongoDB key record before import. RPM trust is machine-wide, unlike a per-repository keyring; gpgcheck=1 requires signed packages but is not repository-metadata signing. Do not bypass verification with --nogpgcheck.[104] sudo dnf install curl gnupg2 python3-dnf-plugin-versionlock curl -fsSLo server-8.0.asc https://pgp.mongodb.com/server-8.0.asc gpg --show-keys --with-fingerprint server-8.0.asc # STOP here until the complete fingerprint has been independently approved. sudo rpm --import server-8.0.asc Create root-owned /etc/yum.repos.d/mongodb-org-8.0.repo (0644). The RHEL 9 repository tab gives this URL; do not substitute the default tab’s RHEL 10 URL.[113] [mongodb-org-8.0] name=MongoDB Repository baseurl=https://repo.mongodb.org/yum/redhat/9/mongodb-org/8.0/x86_64/ gpgcheck=1 enabled=1 gpgkey=https://pgp.mongodb.com/server-8.0.asc The published repository metadata contains these exact NEVRAs: server/router 8.0.29-1.el9.x86_64, shell 2.10.0-1.el8.x86_64, Tools 100.17.0-1.x86_64. The shell’s el8 release tag is actually published in the RHEL 9 repository; do not invent an el9 shell build or infer its NEVRA from its shorter RPM filename. Server/router require OpenSSL 3 and glibc 2.34 symbols; DNF resolves the maintained RHEL dependencies.[106] sudo dnf --refresh --disablerepo='*' --enablerepo=mongodb-org-8.0 \ list --showduplicates mongodb-org-server mongodb-org-mongos mongodb-mongosh mongodb-database-tools sudo dnf install mongodb-org-server-8.0.29-1.el9.x86_64 \ mongodb-mongosh-2.10.0-1.el8.x86_64 mongodb-database-tools-100.17.0-1.x86_64 sudo systemctl disable --now mongod rpm -q mongodb-org-server mongodb-mongosh mongodb-database-tools sudo dnf versionlock add mongodb-org-server mongodb-mongosh mongodb-database-tools sudo dnf versionlock list Review the transaction’s repository/version/signature prompts; omit automatic yes. The server RPM enables boot start on a fresh install, so disable/stop it until bootstrap is accepted. Upgrading an active server package may try to restart it: package work is part of the maintenance window.[100] These are direct components, not a partly pinned metapackage. Install mongodb-org-mongos-8.0.29-1.el9.x86_64 only on router hosts as explained in sharding. If an exact package is unavailable, stop; review a replacement or retrieve an approved retained artifact with signature/checksum verification. Version locks select installed package NEVRAs and need scheduled security review, not permanent neglect.[112]

title: Keep SELinux enforcing
context: Databases · Get a server running · MongoDB · Installation and first start
text: The official policy covers standard RPM/systemd mongod installations on RHEL 9: /usr/bin/mongod, /var/lib/mongo, /var/log/mongodb, /run/mongodb, package user/unit and standard MongoDB ports. It does not cover mongos, shell/tools, arbitrary extra services or relocated paths. Changing those means a site-reviewed policy/integration, not disabling SELinux. The installation manual explicitly warns custom settings are outside the supplied policy’s standard contract.[103][104] Install the documented policy build prerequisites plus RHEL’s management/diagnostic tools. Build as an ordinary user from a reviewed immutable revision; only installation needs sudo. The revision below is the reviewed source, not permission to ignore future policy/security fixes.[103][110] sudo dnf install git make checkpolicy policycoreutils selinux-policy-devel \ policycoreutils-python-utils setools-console audit git clone https://github.com/mongodb/mongodb-selinux cd mongodb-selinux git checkout --detach 18181652362a46fd4511a56f20c4055712deb252 git rev-parse HEAD # Review source/diff and retain its revision with the deployment record. make sudo make install sudo semodule -l sudo restorecon -Rv /usr/bin/mongod /var/lib/mongo /var/log/mongodb sudo restorecon -v /usr/lib/systemd/system/mongod.service /etc/mongod.conf sudo semanage port -l | grep '^mongod_port_t' getenforce Require Enforcing, the installed mongodb policy module, and appropriate port labels before start. After start, inspect ps -eZ for mongod_t and Audit denials, not just an active unit. The policy README’s automatic-application wording is not proof the module is already installed; the versioned RPM spec does not install that policy, so the explicit build/install and readback above remain required.[100][103][108] Custom paths/ports and restore services follow instance policy integration. Keep startup blocked until that host’s confinement and file access have been checked.

Choose a long, unique secret in the organization’s password manager.[7][18] use admin db.createUser({ user: "useradmin", pwd: passwordPrompt(), roles: [{role: "userAdminAnyDatabase", db: "admin"}] }); exit Reconnect authenticated; omit a password value so the shell prompts: mongosh --host 127.0.0.1 --port 27017 --username useradmin --authenticationDatabase admin use admin db.runCommand({connectionStatus: 1, showPrivileges: true}); db.createUser({user: "operator", pwd: passwordPrompt(), roles: [ {role: "clusterAdmin", db: "admin"}, {role: "readWrite", db: "shop"}, {role: "dbAdmin", db: "shop"} ]}); db.createUser({user: "monitor", pwd: passwordPrompt(), roles: [ {role: "clusterMonitor", db: "admin"} ]}); db.createUser({user: "backup", pwd: passwordPrompt(), roles: [ {role: "backup", db: "admin"} ]}); db.createUser({user: "restore", pwd: passwordPrompt(), roles: [ {role: "restore", db: "admin"} ]}); userAdminAnyDatabase can grant powerful roles and must be protected like a superuser, even though it is not the daily data account. operator is a deliberately privileged training/operations identity, not an application login. title: Prove readiness and close bootstrap
context: Databases · Get a server running · MongoDB · Installation and first start
text: mongod --version mongosh --version mongodump --version mongosh --host 127.0.0.1 --port 27017 --username operator --authenticationDatabase admin db.getSiblingDB("admin").runCommand({ping: 1}); db.getSiblingDB("admin").runCommand({getCmdLineOpts: 1}); db.getSiblingDB("shop").getCollectionInfos(); Expected observations: service active, correct binary/tool versions, intended listener/path, authenticated privileged command succeeds. In a separate unauthenticated local shell, a protected operation such as listing shop collections must be rejected. ping alone is not an authorization test. Then enable boot start with sudo systemctl enable mongod.[6][9][104] If first-user creation returns Unauthorized, an existing user/role may already have closed the exception. Authenticate with the existing administrator; do not delete the data directory or open an unauthenticated network listener to “fix” it. If startup fails, preserve logs and use startup diagnosis. Keep a known-good config copy for rollback; a config rollback does not undo created users or application data.[7] Before remote clients, configure TLS and private network access. The loopback bootstrap here is not a remote production connection recipe.

title: Binary distribution alternative
context: Databases · Get a server running · MongoDB · Installation and first start
text: If RPMs cannot be used, select the RHEL 9 x86_64 Community tarball for the approved server version from MongoDB’s archive and verify its official checksum/signature. The RHEL tarball guide lists libcurl, openssl and xz-libs as dependencies (sudo dnf install libcurl openssl xz-libs); shell/Tools remain separate releases. Extract into a versioned directory such as /opt/mongodb/8.0.29. Tarballs create no service account, config, directories or unit: provision these explicitly and keep foreground systemd supervision, limits and glibc environment aligned with the reviewed RPM unit.[101][105] A binary under /opt is outside the standard policy file-context mapping. Before starting, have the SELinux owner review persistent executable/data/log/unit labels and domain transition plus any required narrowly scoped policy. Verify a confined process under enforcing mode on the exact RHEL build. Do not copy the guide’s conflicting generic account paragraph or use an unconfined tarball process as an installation shortcut. The preferred baseline remains vendor RPMs.[103][107][110] Retain the exact artifact and digest in the deployment record. Do not replace /usr/bin/mongod underneath a package-managed service, install an archive for a different OpenSSL/glibc target, or infer that successful extraction proves support. Reuse the same secure bootstrap/readiness checks. Package installation is preferred here because it supplies the integration that the binary path leaves to you.[105][104]

title: Troubleshooting and isolated instances
context: Databases · Get a server running · MongoDB
text: Read-only first. A successful TCP connection proves neither authentication nor replica-set readiness.[6][104] sudo systemctl status mongod --no-pager sudo systemctl cat mongod sudo journalctl -u mongod -n 100 --no-pager sudo ss -ltnp sudo stat /etc/mongod.conf /var/lib/mongo /var/log/mongodb sudo -u mongod test -w /var/lib/mongo sudo -u mongod test -w /var/log/mongodb Inspect /var/log/mongodb/mongod.log as well as the journal. Redact client data, tokens and infrastructure details before sharing logs. Symptom Check Safe next action Unit not found Correct official package; unit search paths systemctl daemon-reload after installing/changing a unit, not after merely editing YAML YAML/unknown-option error Spaces, hierarchy, exact 8.0 option Restore prior config; never solve by deleting all security settings Address already in use Listener/process on chosen port Correct instance port; do not kill an unidentified process Permission denied Service user, every parent directory, log/cert/key permissions Fix only intended owner/path; avoid recursive world-writable permissions DBPathInUse / lock failure Another process using same path Identify owner; do not remove lock files while a server may be alive TLS handshake failure CA chain, SAN hostname, expiry, clocks, client certificate policy Repair trust/identity; never tlsAllowInvalidCertificates as the fix Authentication failure Username, authSource, mechanism, expired/rotated credentials Test a fresh authenticated session; distinguish Unauthorized from bad credentials No primary / selection timeout Member DNS, ports, majority, rs.status() Repair topology/network; direct connection is diagnostic, not an HA fix Disk full / OOM Free space, log growth, cache/resource budget Add capacity or reduce pressure; do not remove WiredTiger/journal files On RHEL 9 check both DAC and SELinux: ownership alone cannot fix a label/domain denial. Use getenforce, ls -ldZ, matchpathcon -V, ps -eZ and sudo ausearch -m AVC,USER_AVC -ts recent. Check auditd if audit results are empty. Repair known labeling/configuration problems first; never use permissive mode or blindly install audit2allow output. bindIp selects local interfaces, not a client allowlist; apply scoped firewalld access.[110] A second process or relocated dbPath is outside the standard RPM policy assumptions. Prefer a separate restore host with the ordinary package layout when you do not have an approved custom integration. The following persistent label mappings are inputs to that integration, not a claim that relabeling alone provides a complete custom policy. Have the SELinux owner inspect the loaded policy, domain transition, parent-directory traversal, runtime and secret access; rehearse startup, shutdown, log rotation and recovery under enforcing mode before authorizing use.[103][104][110] For the same-trust restore instance below, the base MongoDB policy defines these types. Check existing local rules (semanage fcontext -l -C) before adding; if an exact rule exists, inspect it and deliberately modify that rule rather than applying duplicate mappings or overwriting unrelated labels.[107][108] sudo semanage fcontext -l -C sudo semanage fcontext -a -t mongod_var_lib_t '/srv/mongodb/restore(/.*)?' sudo semanage fcontext -a -t mongod_runtime_t '/run/mongodb-restore(/.*)?' sudo semanage fcontext -a -t mongod_unit_file_t '/etc/systemd/system/mongod-restore\.service' sudo restorecon -Rv /srv/mongodb/restore # Run after saving the unit/config; /run directory is created by systemd. sudo restorecon -v /etc/systemd/system/mongod-restore.service /etc/mongod-restore.conf sudo semanage port -l | grep '^mongod_port_t' The pinned policy names runtime type mongod_runtime_t with mongod_var_run_t as an alias. Data needs mongod_var_lib_t; logs need mongod_log_t. The existing /var/log/mongodb(/.*)? mapping includes restore.log. A new log directory needs its own persistent semanage fcontext -a -t mongod_log_t '/chosen/log(/.*)?' and restorecon -Rv /chosen/log, plus ownership and traversable parents. Do not use one transient chcon as a persistent solution.[107][108][110] The base RHEL port type normally already includes TCP 27017–27019. Inspect before adding: the restore port 27018 and shard/config ports 27018/27019 must not be blindly re-added. For a genuinely unassigned custom port, after policy review use, for example, sudo semanage port -a -t mongod_port_t -p tcp 28020. If another service owns the port label, stop and choose/review the conflict; do not steal it with -m. Change YAML, client/member endpoints, firewall and monitoring together. Port labeling is not a firewall rule.[103][105][110] After starting the reviewed service, require mongod_t, the intended runtime/path labels, no unexplained AVC denials, correct effective settings and authenticated allowed/denied operations. sudo -u mongod test -r FILE tests DAC, not the daemon’s SELinux domain. Unconfined execution is not success. A failed custom policy gate means stop the instance and repair/escalate; do not make the whole host permissive.[108][110] For relocated data on a separate mount, add a root-owned drop-in /etc/systemd/system/mongod.service.d/storage.conf: [Unit] RequiresMountsFor=/srv/mongodb/main Configure and verify the mount itself in the platform’s persistent mount configuration. RequiresMountsFor orders/requires known mount units; it does not invent a mount or prove the expected volume is mounted. Check findmnt --target /srv/mongodb/main, filesystem UUID/source/options, ownership and labels before copying and after a controlled reboot. Do not allow startup on an empty underlying root-filesystem directory if a required volume is missing. For extra safety use an approved ConditionPathIsMountPoint on the actual mountpoint when appropriate. Reload systemd after unit/drop-in edits, not for a YAML-only change. Use another standalone instance for a disposable exercise or restore; do not call two processes on one disk “HA.” Independent paths and users do not reserve CPU/RAM/I/O. Set a combined memory budget and use service/cgroup limits only after observing startup and workload behavior.[6][10] Property Main package instance Disposable restore instance Service mongod mongod-restore Config /etc/mongod.conf /etc/mongod-restore.conf dbPath /var/lib/mongo /srv/mongodb/restore Log /var/log/mongodb/mongod.log /var/log/mongodb/restore.log TCP 27017 27018 Bind Loopback until hardened Loopback only OS account mongod mongod in this disposable same-trust example; use separate account for security separation Create a new empty target directory. Never copy a running dbPath into it. On a fresh host create the path first, then apply the persistent mappings above after saving its unit/config; the order matters because restorecon cannot label an absent path.[21][110] sudo install -d -o mongod -g mongod -m 700 /srv/mongodb/restore /etc/mongod-restore.conf: storage: dbPath: /srv/mongodb/restore wiredTiger: engineConfig: cacheSizeGB: 0.5 systemLog: destination: file path: /var/log/mongodb/restore.log logAppend: true net: port: 27018 bindIp: 127.0.0.1 unixDomainSocket: enabled: false security: authorization: enabled The 0.5 GB cache is an explicit small-lab allocation, not a production recommendation or a total memory cap. This same-trust custom unit preserves the RPM foreground/glibc/limit contract; it is not supplied or automatically confined by the RPM. Complete the custom integration gate before starting.[101][103] /etc/systemd/system/mongod-restore.service:[6][10] [Unit] Description=MongoDB isolated restore instance After=network-online.target Wants=network-online.target RequiresMountsFor=/srv/mongodb/restore [Service] Type=simple User=mongod Group=mongod Environment="MONGODB_CONFIG_OVERRIDE_NOFORK=1" Environment="GLIBC_TUNABLES=glibc.pthread.rseq=0" RuntimeDirectory=mongodb-restore RuntimeDirectoryMode=0750 ExecStart=/usr/bin/mongod --config /etc/mongod-restore.conf Restart=no LimitNOFILE=64000 LimitNPROC=64000 LimitMEMLOCK=infinity Limi

Complete the custom integration gate before starting.[101][103] /etc/systemd/system/mongod-restore.service:[6][10] [Unit] Description=MongoDB isolated restore instance After=network-online.target Wants=network-online.target RequiresMountsFor=/srv/mongodb/restore [Service] Type=simple User=mongod Group=mongod Environment="MONGODB_CONFIG_OVERRIDE_NOFORK=1" Environment="GLIBC_TUNABLES=glibc.pthread.rseq=0" RuntimeDirectory=mongodb-restore RuntimeDirectoryMode=0750 ExecStart=/usr/bin/mongod --config /etc/mongod-restore.conf Restart=no LimitNOFILE=64000 LimitNPROC=64000 LimitMEMLOCK=infinity LimitFSIZE=infinity LimitCPU=infinity LimitAS=infinity TasksMax=infinity TimeoutStopSec=infinity [Install] WantedBy=multi-user.target sudo chown root:mongod /etc/mongod-restore.conf sudo chmod 640 /etc/mongod-restore.conf sudo restorecon -v /etc/mongod-restore.conf /etc/systemd/system/mongod-restore.service sudo systemd-analyze verify /etc/systemd/system/mongod-restore.service sudo systemctl daemon-reload # Start only after the custom SELinux/mount checks below are accepted. sudo systemctl start mongod-restore sudo systemctl status mongod-restore --no-pager mongosh --host 127.0.0.1 --port 27018 Run the first-user bootstrap at 27018, creating destination-specific credentials. Do not assume main-instance users exist here. Check getCmdLineOpts, protected access and paths at 27018 before restoring. Do not enable restore-instance boot start; stop it after the drill. Keep authentication enabled even on this isolated instance because other local users may connect.[7][9]

title: Relocate a standalone safely
context: Databases · Get a server running · MongoDB · Troubleshooting and isolated instances
text: Disruptive; physical data copy. This procedure moves one standalone, not a sharded cluster and not a replica-set failover. Have a restorable backup, destination capacity, maintenance window and a recorded old config. Keep the old directory intact until acceptance.[6][21] Quiesce application writes; stop the exact service cleanly. Confirm it stopped and no process uses the old dbPath. Create an empty destination on supported local storage; copy the whole stopped directory, preserving ownership/modes. This example uses /srv/mongodb/main and assumes it did not previously exist. Change only storage.dbPath, plus any required confinement/mount policy. Verify persistent mount availability before boot start. Start and inspect recovery logs, effective path, users, collections/indexes and application read/write checks. sudo systemctl stop mongod sudo systemctl is-active mongod sudo install -d -o mongod -g mongod -m 700 /srv/mongodb/main sudo cp -a /var/lib/mongo/. /srv/mongodb/main/ # STOP on copy error; confirm size/file inventory and intended ownership. sudo semanage fcontext -a -t mongod_var_lib_t '/srv/mongodb/main(/.*)?' sudo restorecon -Rv /srv/mongodb/main # Edit /etc/mongod.conf: storage.dbPath: /srv/mongodb/main # Add the mount dependency/drop-in described below; complete policy review. sudo systemctl daemon-reload sudo systemctl start mongod Inspect the source mount using findmnt --target /var/lib/mongo and target mount using findmnt --target /srv/mongodb/main before the copy. The fcontext addition in this example assumes no existing exact local mapping; use the conflict checks above. An inactive result is expected after stop, but confirm process termination separately before copying. Copy failure means do not start from the partial target. If validation fails before new writes, stop, restore the old path/config and restart. Once new writes have landed at the new location, reverting paths loses them; stop traffic and reconcile/restore instead. Never run both directory copies as competing authoritative servers.[21]

title: Stop and rotate deliberately
context: Databases · Get a server running · MongoDB · Troubleshooting and isolated instances
text: systemctl stop mongod requests orderly shutdown; kill -9 is not normal administration. Inspect systemctl show mongod -p TimeoutStopUSec -p SendSIGKILL: the vendor unit does not specify its own stop timeout, so systemd defaults/drop-ins matter. For shutdowns that need more time, use an approved service drop-in (for example TimeoutStopSec=infinity under [Service]) and a supervised escalation plan; do not assume the default timeout cannot end in SIGKILL.[101] On a replica set, use a secondary-first maintenance plan rather than stopping the primary casually. systemctl restart disconnects clients; driver retry behavior does not make it invisible.[27][104] Default file-log rotation by MongoDB renames the old file and opens a new one. Run as an identity with logRotate privilege (clusterAdmin includes cluster-management capabilities):[43][85] db.getSiblingDB("admin").runCommand({logRotate: 1}); Check the new log receives entries, then compress/archive only the closed old file under retention policy. If integrating OS logrotate with systemLog.logRotate: reopen, also set logAppend: true, rename externally, and issue logRotate; do not mix the two rotation modes or truncate a live log blindly. Logs may contain query data and need restrictive access, rotation and off-host retention appropriate to policy.[43]

title: Relational-to-document migration
context: Databases · Protect it and change it safely · MongoDB
text: A MongoDB migration is an application/data-model migration, not “restore a SQL dump.” Inventory source objects, joins, routines, constraints, collations, identifier generation, transactions and permission assumptions. For this worked model, customers remain referenced documents and bounded order lines embed under each order.[35] Source contract Target decision orders + order_lines join One bounded order aggregate, stable source ID Customer foreign key customerId + tenant check; transaction/application policy and reconciliation DECIMAL totals Decimal128 plus explicit currency/rounding rules BIGINT keys String or BSON Long, consistent in references and filters Auto-increment Preserve source identity during migration; choose future globally unique strategy Case-insensitive uniqueness Deliberate collation/normalization/index policy, checked against duplicates Triggers/procedures Application/service workflow; no automatic SQL translation Relational permissions MongoDB roles on actual resources; no assumption of field/tenant row policy Timestamp without timezone Document original timezone/DST resolution before conversion Document each transformation, including NULL versus missing, empty strings, binary/UUID representation, decimal overflow and invalid dates. Reject/quarantine incompatible rows with source keys and reason; never silently coerce them merely to finish the import.[36][45] Data mutation on a disposable staging database. The source extract must represent a consistent checkpoint across parent/child tables. The following file is authored fixture input, not exported production data. Canonical Extended JSON preserves Decimal128, BSON date and integer types; plain CSV/relaxed JSON can lose important distinctions.[45][46] Create orders.ejson containing one JSON document per line (the single line below is one order): {"_id":"o1001","tenantId":"t1","customerId":"c1","placedAt":{"$date":{"$numberLong":"1788253200000"}},"status":"new","total":{"$numberDecimal":"5.00"},"lines":[{"sku":"pencil","qty":{"$numberInt":"2"},"unitPrice":{"$numberDecimal":"2.50"}}]} Prerequisite: the fixture shop.orders validator exists. As useradmin, grant the loader operator temporary readWrite and dbAdmin roles on shop_migration. Then, authenticated as operator, create a new empty target collection with the same validator and required index; inspect an existing target instead of overwriting it:[18][37][54] const source = db.getSiblingDB("shop"); const stage = db.getSiblingDB("shop_migration"); const definition = source.getCollectionInfos({name: "orders"})[0]; if (!definition) throw new Error("fixture validator missing"); if (stage.getCollectionInfos({name: "orders"}).length) throw new Error("target already exists"); stage.createCollection("orders", { validator: definition.options.validator, validationLevel: "strict", validationAction: "error" }); stage.orders.createIndex({tenantId: 1, placedAt: -1}, {name: "tenant_recent"}); Run the separately verified RHEL 9 x86_64 Database Tools RPM 100.17.0-1 from the OS shell on a trusted worker. It is not a mongod service: give the operator access to its input/output and CA files, not write access to dbPath. Preserve restrictive staging-file modes (umask 077) and review the worker’s actual SELinux domain; the vendor mongod policy does not cover Tools.[103][106] This loopback example matches the initial secured standalone; for the TLS replica/sharded deployment, use its TLS CA and topology URI instead. Keep the target database explicit.[45] mongoimport --host 127.0.0.1 --port 27017 --username operator \ --authenticationDatabase admin --db shop_migration --collection orders \ --type=json --file=orders.ejson --mode=insert --stopOnError --maintainInsertionOrder Require successful exit and inspect the inserted ID/types. --mode=insert intentionally rejects duplicates on a rerun. A failed import can leave earlier documents inserted: inspect/quarantine the partial staging batch, then reload a clean target or use an explicitly designed idempotent upsert strategy. --maintainInsertionOrder makes error stopping immediate; without it a small number of concurrent inserts can still finish after the error. These flags are also checked against the official 100.17.0 tagged option definitions, because the live import manual now describes 100.18.0.[45][67] Option Use / caution --type=json Extended JSON stream; not a SQL dump --jsonArray Only if file is one JSON array; not needed for JSON-lines example --mode=insert New documents; duplicate IDs expose accidental replay --mode=upsert --upsertFields=... Replace matching document; omitted fields can disappear --mode=merge Merge imported fields; may retain unwanted obsolete fields --stopOnError Stop on error; no batch rollback --drop Destructive collection replacement; omitted here to preserve validator/index design CSV typed fields Requires explicit field-type policy; nested arrays/decimals are better represented by a driver/EJSON loader mongoimport does not recreate the entire source database’s indexes, users, roles, views and validation rules. Create/review those separately. Use mongodump/mongorestore for MongoDB logical backup rather than declaring import/export equivalent.[2][45][46] const stage = db.getSiblingDB("shop_migration"); stage.orders.find({_id: "o1001"}).toArray(); stage.orders.aggregate([ {$project: {_id: 1, totalType: {$type: "$total"}, dateType: {$type: "$placedAt"}, quantities: {$map: {input: "$lines", as: "line", in: {$type: "$$line.qty"}}}}} ]).toArray(); stage.orders.aggregate([ {$group: {_id: "$tenantId", orders: {$sum: 1}, amount: {$sum: "$total"}}}, {$sort: {_id: 1}} ]).toArray(); stage.orders.aggregate([ {$project: {_id: 1, total: 1, lineTotal: {$sum: {$map: { input: "$lines", as: "line", in: {$multiply: ["$$line.qty", "$$line.unitPrice"]} }}}}}, {$match: {$expr: {$ne: ["$total", "$lineTotal"]}}} ]).toArray(); For this one-line fixture, acceptance is one o1001, decimal total, date placedAt, int quantities, correct tenant/customer IDs and no line-total mismatch. Real totals may include taxes/discounts/shipping: use the source’s actual business equation, not the simplified fixture equation. Compare count and exact decimal aggregates by tenant/currency/status to the same source checkpoint; retain exception reports.[35][45] Also reconcile orphan references using the tenant-aware lookup, duplicate business keys, date ranges, delete/tombstone behavior and index/validator definitions. The lookup is database-local: for this staging exercise, prepare shop_migration.customers from the same checkpoint, and run the pipeline with db.getSiblingDB("shop_migration"); querying shop.orders would accidentally validate the original fixture instead. For the one-order fixture, staging customer {_id: "c1", tenantId: "t1", name: "Mira"} is sufficient. Inspect existing staging customers before inserting; do not replace a real customer dataset with that example. Byte checksums of a SQL export and BSON file will differ; if using row/document checksums, define deterministic canonical field order, decimal/date/null encoding and the same logical projection on both sides. An inspection export can preserve BSON types in canonical EJSON, but remains data interchange, not a complete backup; --jsonFormat=canonical is present in the pinned 100.17.0 options:[46][68] mongoexport --host 127.0.0.1 --port 27017 --username operator \ --authenticationDatabase admin --db shop_migration --collection orders \ --jsonFormat=canonical --out=orders-roundtrip.ejson Reimport only into another isolated prepared target, then repeat type/business checks. Protect exports like the source database; they contain usable data. For a small migration, a source write outage through extract/load/reconciliation is the simplest complete consistency story. For a large one, use a source-specific CDC mechanism with a durable checkpoint, ordered transactions and delete handling. title: Capture changes and cut over once
context: Databases · Protect it and change it safely · MongoDB · Relational-to-document migration
text: For a small migration, a source write outage through extract/load/reconciliation is the simplest complete consistency story. For a large one, use a source-specific CDC mechanism with a durable checkpoint, ordered transactions and delete handling. MongoDB change streams observe MongoDB changes, not a MySQL binlog; they do not solve source-side CDC automatically. Choose and validate the connector/application approach separately rather than inventing a universal command.[35][40] A controlled CDC cutover has these gates: Take a consistent bulk snapshot with its exact source log/checkpoint position. Retain enough source history for the entire load and catch-up. Load deterministic document IDs; transform parent/child changes with a defined ordering and transaction policy. A late line deletion must not resurrect an old aggregate. Apply deltas idempotently and persist checkpoints only after acknowledged target effects. Track duplicates, dead letters, lag, schema changes and source-log expiration. Shadow-read and run application tests without letting the target become a second uncontrolled writer. Validate sort/collation, pagination, aggregates, authorization, transactions/retries and error behavior. Stop source writers and drain in-flight transactions. Record final source position; wait until target has applied it. Reconcile counts/totals/references at that stable boundary. Switch one controlled application configuration/traffic path to the target; verify reads and guarded writes with stable business request IDs. Fence old writers, retain old source read-only and monitor. Take a protected target backup and complete a restore drill before retiring source artifacts. No-loss dual writes are not achieved by write(source); write(target);: one side can succeed while the other fails. Use a proven transactional-outbox/CDC design with reconciliation, or accept a write outage. Track who owns the authoritative copy at every stage.

title: Rollback is a data decision
context: Databases · Protect it and change it safely · MongoDB · Relational-to-document migration
text: Before target writes, rollback is usually to keep/re-enable the source and discard the isolated failed target after preserving evidence. After target writes, switching back to a stale source loses accepted work. Predefine reverse replication or a reviewed reconciliation/export process, the maximum tolerated divergence and the authority to approve it. Do not overwrite source rows from an unverified MongoDB export or delete migration logs to make totals agree. Retain immutable source checkpoint extracts and transformation version/digests under retention policy. Revoke the loader’s elevated staging roles and remove temporary plaintext exports when acceptance and recovery retention permit. The application migration is done only when business behavior, recovery and access controls work—not when imported row counts look plausible.[18][45]
