title: Settings, accounts, roles and privileges
context: Databases · Work with objects and access · MySQL
text: Command pattern Scope and limits SHOW GLOBAL VARIABLES LIKE 'max_connections'; Global value. SHOW SESSION VARIABLES reports the current session where supported. SET SESSION variable_name=value; Changes this connection if the variable is session-scoped/dynamic. LOCAL means SESSION, not GLOBAL. SET GLOBAL variable_name=value; Requires variable-administration privilege; global changes to dual-scope variables usually affect newly created sessions, not existing session copies. SET PERSIST variable_name=value; Changes the runtime global value and persists it in server-managed mysqld-auto.cnf if supported. SET PERSIST_ONLY variable_name=value; Persists without changing the runtime value; useful for allowed startup-only settings, with appropriate privilege. RESET PERSIST variable_name; Removes a persisted entry; does not revert its current runtime value. Restore runtime separately or restart with intended configuration. Read the variable’s scope, dynamic status, units and privilege requirements before setting it. Do not hand-edit mysqld-auto.cnf as a routine config workflow. Save prior values, change one thing, and verify both runtime and intended restart behavior. An account is 'user'@'host'; use quoted explicit host identities. mysql.user includes User, Host, plugin, authentication data and static global privileges, but is not the complete representation of roles/dynamic privileges. Do not directly update grant tables or expose authentication strings. A bounded example uses a random server-generated password instead of embedding a secret. The returned credential must be delivered through a secure channel, not copied into logs or this document: CREATE USER 'app_reader'@'192.0.2.10' IDENTIFIED BY RANDOM PASSWORD REQUIRE SSL; ALTER USER 'app_reader'@'192.0.2.10' ACCOUNT LOCK; ALTER USER 'app_reader'@'192.0.2.10' ACCOUNT UNLOCK; 192.0.2.10 is an example address to replace with the actual trusted application host. Locking prevents new authentication; separately review existing sessions if revoking access urgently. CREATE ROLE 'app_read'; GRANT SELECT ON app.* TO 'app_read'; GRANT 'app_read' TO 'app_reader'@'192.0.2.10'; SET DEFAULT ROLE 'app_read' TO 'app_reader'@'192.0.2.10'; SHOW GRANTS FOR 'app_reader'@'192.0.2.10'; Operation Explanation GRANT 'role1', 'role2' TO 'user_name'@'host'; Grants previously created roles to an account. SET DEFAULT ROLE ... TO ... Sets default activation, subject to authority over the target account; not the same as granting the role. SET ROLE NONE; / SET ROLE DEFAULT; Changes active roles in the current session. SELECT CURRENT_ROLE(); Reports current active roles. SHOW GRANTS; / SHOW GRANTS FOR CURRENT_USER; Displays grants for the current account. USING can include named granted roles in the displayed effective privileges. GRANT SELECT(column1, column2), INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE, CREATE, DROP ON app.table_name TO 'user'@'host'; Schematic mixed column/table grant: only SELECT is column-scoped here. Grant only privileges actually required, not this entire list by habit. GRANT ALL ON app.* TO 'user'@'host' WITH GRANT OPTION; Schema-wide privileges plus delegation; not global administrator authority. High impact: reserve for an approved schema owner, not an app reader. REVOKE SELECT ON app.table_name FROM 'user'@'host'; Removes that explicit grant; role/schema/global paths can still give access. DROP USER 'user1'@'host', 'user2'@'host'; Removes accounts; first inventory definers, jobs and connections. Does not drop their application tables. CREATE USER and GRANT are separate operations in 8.4. They take effect without FLUSH PRIVILEGES. mysql_config_editor set --login-path=maintenance --host=localhost --user=operator --password mysql_config_editor print --all mysql --login-path=maintenance mysql_config_editor remove --login-path=maintenance The set command prompts for the password. print masks passwords, not a plaintext credentials listing. Login paths are obfuscation, not strong encryption; someone with sufficient local access can recover them. Protect the file/account and prefer a managed secret mechanism where policy requires one. Named --login-path=maintenance is not redundant. Client option precedence and [client] behavior differ from merely saving arbitrary path names. Use the documented Unix init-file method in a scheduled outage with local OS administrator access, console access, backups and an identified account host. Do not use pkill mysql or start another daemon on a live datadir. Determine the actual unit, executable, option files, datadir and service OS identity. Stop the one intended instance normally and verify it is stopped. Prepare a temporary file containing the authorized account-change SQL using a securely supplied new secret; only the administrator and required service identity may read it. Keep it out of shell history, backups, generic /tmp, and source control. The file is a secret, not a downloadable example. Start that instance under its normal OS user/configuration with the documented --init-file override. Under systemd, choose a temporary unit override appropriate to the installed unit rather than bypassing it blindly. Read the error log and confirm the intended account change. Remove the secret file and temporary startup override, perform a normal controlled restart and verify normal authenticated access. Check that no recovery options remain. The alternative --skip-grant-tables method disables authorization and normally disables networking. Even then local users are a threat: isolate the host/socket and use the official recovery sequence (FLUSH PRIVILEGES before account-management SQL). Never leave this mode running or treat it as routine account administration. If normal startup fails, preserve the original datadir/configuration and investigate; do not reinitialize. [5][21][37][38][39][40][41]

text: MySQL Enterprise Audit is commercial. Use the plugin and installation SQL shipped with the same server distribution/build. title: Logical backups, restore tests and point-in-time recovery
context: Databases · Back up, then restore · MySQL
text: Term Meaning and caveat Cold backup Server stopped cleanly while a consistent copy is taken; not merely a running database with locks. Warm backup Some activity blocked, such as writes/table access, during copying; define the exact locks and engines involved. Hot/online backup Server remains running; may still take brief locks or constrain DDL. “Hot” does not promise zero blocking. Restore Reconstruct files/objects/data from a backup into a selected instance. Recovery Apply the necessary redo/binlog or other recovery steps to reach a consistent state or chosen time; not only salvaging damaged files. [43][45][78][137] Choose a plan against explicit recovery-point (RPO) and recovery-time (RTO) objectives, failure domains, cost and operational complexity. Keep consistent full backups and supported incremental/log chains, protected off-host copies, recoverable keys, monitoring and a practiced incident runbook. Test isolated restores regularly and measure the achieved recovery point/time. A replica or cluster can improve availability but can also replicate deletion or corruption. It is not an independent historical backup. Managed services (the source named Amazon Aurora MySQL) have their own engine versions, backup/restore and regional failover contracts; this self-managed MySQL 8.4 guide does not certify them or promise simplified recovery. Verify the chosen service’s official documentation separately. Logical backups preserve object definitions and/or data in logical form. A SQL dump contains SQL statements; CSV or other delimited data files are not SQL and need their own schema, encoding, NULL/escaping and loader contract. Neither is a physical copy of all server state. [137][138][43] mysqldump option Meaning in the 8.4 client -A, --all-databases Dumps selected server databases subject to tool exclusions/privileges; not a physical image of all server state or external keys/configuration. -B, --databases db1 db2 Includes database-selection and creation statements for named databases. -R, --routines Include stored procedures/functions; inspect definers and required target privileges. -E, --events Include scheduled events; control event execution during restore validation. --triggers Include triggers (enabled by default); target version/privileges still matter. --single-transaction Starts a consistent transaction for transactional tables and disables --lock-tables; not consistent for changing MyISAM/MEMORY data. Avoid concurrent DDL such as ALTER/DROP/RENAME/TRUNCATE during the dump. --lock-all-tables Holds a global read lock across the dump; conflicts with --single-transaction and blocks writes. Plan an outage/lock window. --set-gtid-purged=OFF Omits the GTID-purged and related sql_log_bin manipulation. Whether restored changes receive GTIDs depends on target logging/GTID configuration; it does not simply “make a backup safe.” --ignore-table=db1.tb1 Exclude exactly that qualified table; repeat the option for another table. No trailing comma or comma-separated list. --add-drop-database Adds destructive DROP DATABASE before CREATE statements where applicable. Avoid for merges/production imports; not inherently a replication requirement. --no-create-db Suppresses CREATE DATABASE statements normally added with --databases / --all-databases. --no-create-info Data without CREATE TABLE statements; not a complete independently restorable dump. --no-data Definitions without rows. --source-data=1 / =2 Records source file/position as an active CHANGE REPLICATION SOURCE TO statement or a comment. Can require a brief global read lock even with --single-transaction. Replaces historical --master-data. --compact Enables a set of reduced-output options, not just comment removal; inspect its effects on DROP/LOCK/charset statements. Pipe through pv -trb Optional separate Unix utility reports elapsed time/rate/bytes, not database restore correctness. Pipe through gzip Actually compresses the byte stream. A .gz filename alone does not compress it. > file.sql Shell redirection overwrites a file. Use unique controlled filenames and restrictive permissions. A timestamp naming example should avoid colons when files cross platforms. Example for an existing all-InnoDB app schema, a trusted TLS endpoint, no concurrent DDL, and a least-privilege dump account provisioned for the chosen flags. db.example.com, CA path and output path are site inputs. Bash/EL9 only: umask 077 set -o pipefail mysqldump --host=db.example.com --user=backup --password \ --ssl-mode=VERIFY_IDENTITY --ssl-ca=/etc/mysql/trust/ca.pem \ --single-transaction --routines --events --triggers \ --set-gtid-purged=OFF --databases app \ | gzip > "app-$(date +%Y%m%dT%H%M%S).sql.gz" This example is for a logical application restore, not an automatic GTID replica seed. Record the command/options, server/client versions, object inventory, completion/exit status and checksums. A failed pipeline can leave a partial file; quarantine it. For replication/PITR, separately capture the matching snapshot coordinates/GTID set using the documented consistency procedure. Required privileges can include SELECT, SHOW VIEW, TRIGGER, EVENT, routine visibility, and others depending on tablespaces, locks and GTID options; do not grant ALL merely to suppress an error. mysqlpump was removed in MySQL 8.4. The original mysqlpump -B db1 db2 > pump.sql and queue options are not 8.4 commands. --parallel-schemas=4:db1,db2 historically selected a schema queue; --default-parallelism=4 selected the default queue. Preserve that distinction when interpreting old jobs, but migrate them to a supported dump tool and retest restore format. Thread count should be benchmarked against source, network and destination capacity, not assumed equal to physical cores. Verify file integrity, decompression, manifest and successful dump completion. Encryption keys, config and routine/account dependencies need separate retention. Restore into an isolated disposable server, normally using original schema names. mysql --database=test < dump.sql does not redirect statements containing CREATE DATABASE, USE, fully-qualified names or DROP commands into test. Review the dump before import, isolate replication/events/outbound integrations, and authenticate with a prompted password and verified TLS where TCP is used. For a compressed SQL dump, decompress deliberately and check both decompressor and client exit statuses; use pipefail for pipelines. Check object definitions, definers, row counts/checksums where appropriate, constraints, routines and application business queries. mysqlcheck --user=operator --password --databases app checks supported table operations; it is not a proof of logical/business consistency. Record restore duration against RTO and recoverable point against RPO. See the physical-backup chapter. Binlog format Meaning STATEMENT Records SQL with replication context. title: Point-in-time recovery with binary logs
context: Databases · Back up, then restore · MySQL · Logical backups, restore tests and point-in-time recovery
text: Binlog format Meaning STATEMENT Records SQL with replication context. Some statements are unsafe/nondeterministic; NOW() specifically has replication handling and is not by itself a valid blanket example of failure. ROW Records row-change events; default in 8.4. Generally avoids statement nondeterminism but volume depends on workload/row-image settings. MIXED Switches from statement to row events for cases classified unsafe; does not make arbitrary multi-source writes conflict-free. Use SHOW BINARY LOGS; to inventory available logs and SHOW BINARY LOG STATUS; for current coordinates; neither guarantees a complete archived chain. A full backup plus every required binlog after its consistent boundary is needed. Archive securely off-host and retain source identity, checksums and encryption keys. Restore the base backup to an isolated target. Establish its exact snapshot coordinates/GTID state and which transactions already exist there. Inspect binlogs to identify the last complete transaction before the unwanted event. Time filters use the tool’s interpreted timestamps/timezone and are for locating events; pin validated event/transaction boundaries by file and position for final recovery. Generate a replay stream from all required files in original order. mysqlbinlog --start-position=... --stop-position=... applies the starting limit to the first file and the stopping limit to the last. Resolve these integers from actual logs; no universal numbers are supplied. Replay the normal executable output through mysql in a controlled session, checking both exit statuses and stopping on error. Test this exact boundary on the disposable target before production cutover. Do not add a database filter without understanding cross-database statements/row-event filtering. Reconcile resulting data, users/routines/events and application invariants, then plan cutover and retained rollback. Never replay the bad transaction merely to close a gap. mysqlbinlog option/topic Correct use --start-datetime, --stop-datetime Locate an interval; establish timezone and complete transaction boundaries before accepting a recovery point. --start-position, --stop-position Byte/event positions, not transaction IDs; validate against named files. --read-from-remote-server Retrieve logs through the server, including encrypted logs the server can decrypt. Use authorized credentials and identity-verified TLS. --include-gtids, --exclude-gtids Filter GTID sets for applicable recovery/migration tasks, not “replication only.” Audit missing and duplicate transactions carefully. Existing GTID execution state influences replay. -v, --verbose Adds decoded row commentary for inspection. --base64-output=DECODE-ROWS Diagnostic pseudo-SQL comments, not a replay stream for row changes. Default AUTO retains executable BINLOG event payloads. NEVER also disables required row-event output. /*! ... */ MySQL executable/version comments; do not strip them from a replay/dump assuming every comment is inert.

title: Retention is not reset
context: Databases · Back up, then restore · MySQL · Logical backups, restore tests and point-in-time recovery
text: RESET BINARY LOGS AND GTIDS destroys binlog history and clears GTID execution state; it is not part of routine backup, replica setup or error repair. Do not run it on a source needed by replicas/PITR. If rebuilding a deliberately disposable instance, follow its complete provisioning procedure instead. PURGE BINARY LOGS TO 'file' removes logs before the named file; BEFORE 'timestamp' removes logs older than a cutoff. These are destructive retention operations, not recovery commands. Before choosing a boundary, verify archived copies and restore tests, all connected/disconnected replica needs, delayed replicas, backup coordinates and the recovery-retention policy. NOW() is not a safe generic cutoff. Use server-managed expiry aligned with these dependencies; never delete binary logs using filesystem commands. [43][44][46][47][86][92][95][96][153][156]

title: mydumper / myloader
context: Databases · Back up, then restore · MySQL · Logical backups, restore tests and point-in-time recovery
text: These are third-party parallel logical tools, not Oracle mysqldump aliases. Their own project documentation/release notes govern compatibility. Before deployment pin the exact MyDumper release, read its matching help, authenticate through a restricted configuration or documented prompt mechanism, and test dump/load with that same release. A versionless password-on-command-line recipe is intentionally not provided. Original option/task Review before using -u, --user Authentication identity; provide only needed dump/load privileges. -p, --password Tool-specific password handling; avoid literal command-line secrets and verify whether the selected version supports a prompt/config mechanism. -t, --threads Parallel workers; budget source locks/snapshot consistency and target I/O. mydumper -B, --database Database selection; the original -d as database was wrong for current MyDumper. mydumper -o, --outputdir New protected dump output directory. myloader -d, --directory Input dump directory; not a database-selection flag. Select snapshot/locking behavior for all table engines; a fast multi-threaded dump is not automatically a consistent one. Preserve metadata files and check both tools’ completion status, then restore/reconcile in isolation. See the project documentation rather than borrowing Shell or mysqlpump queue syntax.

title: MySQL Shell 8.4 utilities
context: Databases · Back up, then restore · MySQL · Logical backups, restore tests and point-in-time recovery
text: MySQL Shell is a separately installed tool; these calls use its JavaScript mode (\js), not SQL in mysql. The pinned Oracle-hosted 8.4 manual is used because the public /mysql-shell/8.4/ URLs now redirect to a newer manual. Use an 8.4 Shell maintenance build compatible with the source and destination and record its actual version. Task JavaScript call pattern Instance dump util.dumpInstance('/backup/instance', {threads:4, consistent:true}) Schema dump util.dumpSchemas(['app'], '/backup/app', {threads:4, consistent:true}) Table dump util.dumpTables('app', ['customers','orders'], '/backup/tables') HeatWave-targeted dump util.dumpInstance('/backup/heatwave', {threads:4, ocimds:true, consistent:true}) after checking HeatWave’s current migration requirements. Load Shell dump util.loadDump('/backup/app') against the deliberately selected isolated destination. This does not load a mysqldump SQL file. Use new/empty writable output directories and a properly authenticated Shell session. Do not put connection passwords in JS source. The loader creates objects and inserts data; establish target privileges, free space, existing-object/GTID policy and restore isolation first. Option Meaning ocimds Real 8.4 option for HeatWave compatibility checks/adjustments. Not required for ordinary MySQL-to-MySQL backup and not a generic “safer” switch. threads Total parallel worker connections (default 4); not mysqlpump’s per-schema queues. consistent Default true. Establishes synchronized consistent snapshots under initial read/table locks and uses a backup lock where available; does not normally hold all tables read-locked throughout the data copy. Engine/DDL/privilege restrictions still apply; false can create inconsistent dumps. Inspect documented required privileges and consistency-check failures. Avoid ignoreVersion or compatibility transformations as unexplained workarounds; record every transformation and test the loaded result. [95][96][101][102]

title: Physical backups, tablespace transfer and log rotation
context: Databases · Back up, then restore · MySQL
text: Physical backups are server-format dependent. title: Transport an InnoDB file-per-table tablespace
context: Databases · Back up, then restore · MySQL · Physical backups, tablespace transfer and log rotation
text: This is a restricted table-transfer workflow, not a general full backup. Verify the documented source/target version, page size, row format, partition, encryption and foreign-key restrictions. Create the exact matching definition on the destination first and ensure its existing data is disposable/backed up. General/system tablespace tables cannot be treated as arbitrary standalone .ibd files. On the source, keep one session open with FLUSH TABLES app.table_name FOR EXPORT;. This is a SQL lock held by that session; do not disconnect before copying. While the lock is held, use an OS file-copy tool to copy the matching .ibd and export .cfg files to protected staging. For encrypted tables, follow the documented .cfp/key transfer requirements too. Verify the copy and only then UNLOCK TABLES; in the source session. cp is not SQL. On the destination, create the exact table definition, then ALTER TABLE app.table_name DISCARD TABLESPACE; only for the intended empty/disposable table. This discards its current tablespace; do not apply it to a populated production table. Copy the staged table files into the destination table’s actual schema path, apply correct MySQL ownership/permissions/SELinux context, and verify compatibility before ALTER TABLE app.table_name IMPORT TABLESPACE;. Read import warnings/errors, compare definition/row counts/data and relevant foreign-key relationships, then test application queries. Keep the source/export until validation is complete; do not delete production source data because import returned success. The source’s missing destination file-copy step is essential. Quiesce related tables together when consistency spans relationships; independent exports are not an atomic multi-table backup. [48]

title: Rotate text logs, not database recovery files
context: Databases · Back up, then restore · MySQL · Physical backups, tablespace transfer and log rotation
text: On EL9 use the package’s existing logrotate configuration as the starting point. Confirm whether the error log goes to a file, journald or a configured log component. FLUSH ERROR LOGS and FLUSH SLOW LOGS require suitable privileges and apply only to the matching file logging setup; logrotate does not restart arbitrary logging components. Original directive Meaning and deployment check /var/log/mysql/mysql_error.log /var/log/mysql/slow_query.log Example paths only; use actual configured paths. EL9 RPM error-log defaults often differ. Avoid duplicate stanzas managed by the package. compress Compress rotated text files; consider delaycompress until the server has reopened the new file successfully. create 660 mysql mysql Mode/owner/group of the new file. Prefer only the readers required by policy; 0640 may suffice. Verify service access and SELinux labels. size 1G Rotate when size exceeds this threshold at a scheduled logrotate run; not a hard maximum enforced continuously. dateext Date-based archive naming; frequent rotations may need adequate date granularity. missingok, notifempty Tolerate absent/empty files; do not use these to hide missing required audit data. sharedscripts Run the reopen action once for the grouped files. postrotate / endscript Reopen logs via an authorized local MySQL connection; ensure the scheduled OS identity can access the intended restricted login path/socket. An operator’s personal login path is not automatically root’s or the service user’s. rotate 30 Keep up to 30 rotated files, not necessarily 30 days; align with retention/security requirements. Inspect logrotate’s dry-run/debug output with the real local configuration, then perform a controlled test: server must write to the new file and archives must remain readable by authorized operators. Do not place credentials in the stanza. Do not send binlogs, relay logs, redo, undo, .ibd or Enterprise Audit files through this generic text-log recipe; they have their own managed retention/rotation interfaces. [19][29][42][47][143]

title: Client workflow and moving the data directory
context: Databases · Get a server running · MySQL
text: In the mysql interactive client, these are client commands, not SQL sent through a connector: prompt (\u@\h) [\d]>\_ tee /secure/operator/mysql-session.log SELECT NOW(); SELECT DATABASE(); notee \u, \h and \d expand user, host and current database; \_ is a space. tee appends statements/output to the named local file. Create a private directory and restrict file access before using it; account changes, query results and personal data can leak into transcripts. notee, not NOTEEE, stops logging. Do not use session logging during secret-entry/recovery operations. EL9 RPM service; planned outage. Have a tested backup, a rollback window, console access and capacity for both old and new copies. A raw filesystem copy while MySQL is writing is not a consistent backup. External tablespaces, keyring data, log files and certificates may live outside @@datadir; inventory them separately. Record the active datadir, all related file paths, server UUID/version, option files, ownership/ACLs/extended attributes, SELinux contexts, service restrictions and mount dependencies. Select an empty destination, for example /srv/mysql-data, not a directory already containing another instance. Stop the exact instance through systemd; verify no process is using its datadir and that shutdown completed. Prevent accidental restart during copying. Do not kill unrelated clients or servers. Copy contents of /var/lib/mysql/ into /srv/mysql-data/, preserving numeric owners, modes, links, ACLs and xattrs. On EL9 a suitable tool is rsync -aHAX --numeric-ids /var/lib/mysql/ /srv/mysql-data/ while stopped. The trailing slash is intentional; cp -r /var/lib/mysql /newpath may instead create /newpath/mysql and lose required metadata. Verify the copied file set/metadata and offline checksums while both remain unchanged. Do not recursively make every file executable with chmod -R 750; use directory and file permissions appropriate to their existing roles, with private keys restricted. Change the intended datadir option and any deliberately moved socket/log/PID paths. Update only needed client settings, SELinux exact-path contexts, mount/service access and backup tooling. Apply persistent file-context mappings and restore labels, not just temporary chcon changes. Validate configuration, start the intended instance, inspect error logs and verify @@datadir, expected schemas/data, encryption/key access, application behavior and replication/backup jobs. Do not allow the first start to initialize a mistakenly empty/unmounted target. Keep the original stopped copy until verification and rollback retention complete. If rolling back before accepting new writes, stop the new instance, restore old path/config/policy and start the old copy. After new writes, switching back loses them: reconcile/recover them under a planned rollback, not a blind path reversal. Do not delete the old datadir as part of the first successful startup. title: Configuration and systemd services
context: Databases · Get a server running · MySQL
text: Review the complete configuration appendix before adapting settings. On the selected RPM platform /etc/my.cnf is a normal option-file location; included files, command-line options and mysqld-auto.cnf can also affect effective settings. mysqld --verbose --help reports option-file search locations and recognized options. Use mysqld --validate-config with the intended configuration before a maintenance restart; it is not a storage/permissions/replication health test. Keep a restricted backup of the effective option files. Edit a reviewed local copy, preserve ownership/mode, inspect a diff, and deploy deliberately. Do not download a blog file straight into /etc. Use the installed RPM’s mysqld.service. Read it and its overrides first: systemctl cat mysqld.service systemctl show mysqld.service -p FragmentPath -p DropInPaths -p User -p Group Prefer a narrow systemctl edit mysqld.service drop-in over replacing the vendor unit in /usr/lib/systemd/system. A complete unit in /etc/systemd/system shadows vendor updates and makes you responsible for maintaining the entire unit. systemctl daemon-reload reloads unit definitions, not MySQL option files; a server restart is separately planned. The single-instance unit appendix explains the source unit’s invalid EnvironmentFile assignment and package-specific pre-start helper. The multiple-instance template explains %I, suffix groups and unique paths. Generic tarball installations need their own tested service integration; they cannot assume RPM helper paths. This is a same-host, same-version cold move of the existing default instance from /var/lib/mysql to an approved empty /srv/mysql-data, not a clone, upgrade or live rsync backup. Keep the original directory unchanged for rollback. A separate new instance has different UUID/identity requirements. Rehearse this move and restore the backup before the production window. Record effective datadir, socket, PID, error/binlog/relay/undo/tablespace/keyring paths and server_uuid; locate external files and absolute paths in configuration/log index files. A directory copy does not relocate every dependency. If external tablespaces or absolute log paths are present, retain accessible paths or follow their documented move procedure; do not edit managed data files speculatively. Back up data, keys, config, unit overrides, SELinux customizations and client/backup connection settings. Quiesce writers and scheduled jobs, stop the exact unit with sudo systemctl stop mysqld.service, and confirm it is inactive and no process still owns the datadir. Confirm clean shutdown in the error log. Never copy changing InnoDB files and call that a cold backup. Provision and verify the intended destination filesystem/mount, free space, ACL/xattr support and ownership. The destination must be empty intentionally, not an absent mount. For approved directories, inspect the dry run, then copy the stopped tree: sudo rsync -aHAXn --numeric-ids /var/lib/mysql/ /srv/mysql-data/ # Only after reviewing the dry run and confirming the server is stopped: sudo rsync -aHAX --numeric-ids /var/lib/mysql/ /srv/mysql-data/ sudo rsync -aHAXnrc --numeric-ids /var/lib/mysql/ /srv/mysql-data/ Check every exit status and investigate any content difference in the checksum comparison; no --delete is used. This preserves metadata where the destination supports it, but copied SELinux xattrs must then be reconciled with the new persistent path policy. With policycoreutils-python-utils installed, inspect semanage fcontext -l -C and matchpathcon first. If no conflicting local mapping exists, use an equivalence mapping so the relocated tree inherits the standard datadir’s differentiated socket/file rules, rather than assigning one type to every file: sudo semanage fcontext -a -e /var/lib/mysql /srv/mysql-data sudo restorecon -Rv /srv/mysql-data ls -ldZ /srv/mysql-data Existing mappings require reviewed modification, not another blind -a. Verify database files use mysqld_db_t and the configured socket/PID use mysqld_var_run_t; error logs use mysqld_log_t. Keep the standard /var/log/mysqld.log in this move. A custom log or runtime directory needs its own mapping and permissions, not the data-directory type. Change the intended option group to datadir=/srv/mysql-data and socket=/srv/mysql-data/mysql.sock; update the intended clients/backup/monitoring socket settings. Preserve auto.cnf for this same instance. Keep PID/error-log locations unchanged unless separately planned. In /etc/sysconfig/mysql, preserve other values and set NO_INIT=true for the initialized instance, reviewing its effect on other units. Add a narrow systemctl edit mysqld.service drop-in: [Unit] RequiresMountsFor=/srv/mysql-data This orders/requires the mounts necessary to access the path; it does not prove the correct volume or database is present. Confirm the expected volume and retained data explicitly. Reload systemd definitions, validate server configuration, and start the intended unit. Do not start a second service over the old directory while validating the new one. Inspect the unit journal/MySQL log, getenforce, ls -lZ for newly created socket/PID, and relevant AVCs. Connect explicitly to the new socket and check @@datadir, @@socket, @@server_uuid, object/data invariants and replication state. Test application traffic, a fresh backup/restore and boot/mount failure behavior before retiring the old path. On failure before new writes, stop the new-path unit, restore prior option files/drop-in/socket clients and the previous environment setting, then restart only the unchanged old instance. Remove only the SELinux mapping introduced by this change if abandoning the destination. If new writes were accepted, the old directory is stale: reconcile/restore current data before reverting. Never reverse-copy a live tree or leave two active writers as rollback. [19][20][21][154][161][163][157][106] Historical source example for reading, not a tested procedure or executable download. Applies to MySQL Server 8.4 LTS; the production baseline is RHEL 9 x86_64 with Oracle MySQL Community RPMs from the MySQL Yum repository. Separately licensed products and other platforms are identified explicitly.[1][72] Target: Oracle MySQL 8.4 LTS RPMs on RHEL 9 x86-64. Start from the package’s installed configuration, not an old blog download. The historical file below is retained in full for comparison, not deployment. For a deliberately new single instance with the RPM’s standard datadir/socket/error-log locations, this fragment documents the identity/path choices. It is not a complete production performance, replication or encryption configuration: [mysqld] user=mysql datadir=/var/lib/mysql socket=/var/lib/mysql/mysql.sock log-error=/var/log/mysqld.log bind_address=127.0.0.1 [client] socket=/var/lib/mysql/mysql.sock A TCP loopback bind does not configure every additional listener (for example X Protocol); inventory those separately. Add the narrow approved bind address, firewall and TLS requirements before remote use. Verify mounts and existing data before starting; an empty wrong path can be initialized as a new instance by package helpers. Source option/group Review and replacement guidance innodb_buffer_pool_size=5600M; 70%/10% comments Not a portable default. Measure memory limits/working set, connection buffers, other services and OS headroom; 128 MiB is the ordinary small default unless other sizing automation changes it. disable_log_bin Disables binary logging and breaks ordinary binlog replication/PITR. title: Option files
context: Databases · Get a server running · MySQL · Configuration and systemd services
text: Review the complete configuration appendix before adapting settings. On the selected RPM platform /etc/my.cnf is a normal option-file location; included files, command-line options and mysqld-auto.cnf can also affect effective settings. mysqld --verbose --help reports option-file search locations and recognized options. Use mysqld --validate-config with the intended configuration before a maintenance restart; it is not a storage/permissions/replication health test. Keep a restricted backup of the effective option files. Edit a reviewed local copy, preserve ownership/mode, inspect a diff, and deploy deliberately. Do not download a blog file straight into /etc.

title: Vendor systemd units and overrides
context: Databases · Get a server running · MySQL · Configuration and systemd services
text: Use the installed RPM’s mysqld.service. Read it and its overrides first: systemctl cat mysqld.service systemctl show mysqld.service -p FragmentPath -p DropInPaths -p User -p Group Prefer a narrow systemctl edit mysqld.service drop-in over replacing the vendor unit in /usr/lib/systemd/system. A complete unit in /etc/systemd/system shadows vendor updates and makes you responsible for maintaining the entire unit. systemctl daemon-reload reloads unit definitions, not MySQL option files; a server restart is separately planned. The single-instance unit appendix explains the source unit’s invalid EnvironmentFile assignment and package-specific pre-start helper. The multiple-instance template explains %I, suffix groups and unique paths. Generic tarball installations need their own tested service integration; they cannot assume RPM helper paths.

title: Relocate an existing RHEL RPM instance without reinitializing it
context: Databases · Get a server running · MySQL · Configuration and systemd services
text: This is a same-host, same-version cold move of the existing default instance from /var/lib/mysql to an approved empty /srv/mysql-data, not a clone, upgrade or live rsync backup. Keep the original directory unchanged for rollback. A separate new instance has different UUID/identity requirements. Rehearse this move and restore the backup before the production window. Record effective datadir, socket, PID, error/binlog/relay/undo/tablespace/keyring paths and server_uuid; locate external files and absolute paths in configuration/log index files. A directory copy does not relocate every dependency. If external tablespaces or absolute log paths are present, retain accessible paths or follow their documented move procedure; do not edit managed data files speculatively. Back up data, keys, config, unit overrides, SELinux customizations and client/backup connection settings. Quiesce writers and scheduled jobs, stop the exact unit with sudo systemctl stop mysqld.service, and confirm it is inactive and no process still owns the datadir. Confirm clean shutdown in the error log. Never copy changing InnoDB files and call that a cold backup. Provision and verify the intended destination filesystem/mount, free space, ACL/xattr support and ownership. The destination must be empty intentionally, not an absent mount. For approved directories, inspect the dry run, then copy the stopped tree: sudo rsync -aHAXn --numeric-ids /var/lib/mysql/ /srv/mysql-data/ # Only after reviewing the dry run and confirming the server is stopped: sudo rsync -aHAX --numeric-ids /var/lib/mysql/ /srv/mysql-data/ sudo rsync -aHAXnrc --numeric-ids /var/lib/mysql/ /srv/mysql-data/ Check every exit status and investigate any content difference in the checksum comparison; no --delete is used. This preserves metadata where the destination supports it, but copied SELinux xattrs must then be reconciled with the new persistent path policy. With policycoreutils-python-utils installed, inspect semanage fcontext -l -C and matchpathcon first. If no conflicting local mapping exists, use an equivalence mapping so the relocated tree inherits the standard datadir’s differentiated socket/file rules, rather than assigning one type to every file: sudo semanage fcontext -a -e /var/lib/mysql /srv/mysql-data sudo restorecon -Rv /srv/mysql-data ls -ldZ /srv/mysql-data Existing mappings require reviewed modification, not another blind -a. Verify database files use mysqld_db_t and the configured socket/PID use mysqld_var_run_t; error logs use mysqld_log_t. Keep the standard /var/log/mysqld.log in this move. A custom log or runtime directory needs its own mapping and permissions, not the data-directory type. Change the intended option group to datadir=/srv/mysql-data and socket=/srv/mysql-data/mysql.sock; update the intended clients/backup/monitoring socket settings. Preserve auto.cnf for this same instance. Keep PID/error-log locations unchanged unless separately planned. In /etc/sysconfig/mysql, preserve other values and set NO_INIT=true for the initialized instance, reviewing its effect on other units. Add a narrow systemctl edit mysqld.service drop-in: [Unit] RequiresMountsFor=/srv/mysql-data This orders/requires the mounts necessary to access the path; it does not prove the correct volume or database is present. Confirm the expected volume and retained data explicitly. Reload systemd definitions, validate server configuration, and start the intended unit. Do not start a second service over the old directory while validating the new one. Inspect the unit journal/MySQL log, getenforce, ls -lZ for newly created socket/PID, and relevant AVCs. Connect explicitly to the new socket and check @@datadir, @@socket, @@server_uuid, object/data invariants and replication state. Test application traffic, a fresh backup/restore and boot/mount failure behavior before retiring the old path. On failure before new writes, stop the new-path unit, restore prior option files/drop-in/socket clients and the previous environment setting, then restart only the unchanged old instance. Remove only the SELinux mapping introduced by this change if abandoning the destination. If new writes were accepted, the old directory is stale: reconcile/restore current data before reverting. Never reverse-copy a live tree or leave two active writers as rollback. [19][20][21][154][161][163][157][106]

title: Minimal local-only starting fragment
context: Databases · Get a server running · MySQL · Configuration and systemd services
text: For a deliberately new single instance with the RPM’s standard datadir/socket/error-log locations, this fragment documents the identity/path choices. It is not a complete production performance, replication or encryption configuration: [mysqld] user=mysql datadir=/var/lib/mysql socket=/var/lib/mysql/mysql.sock log-error=/var/log/mysqld.log bind_address=127.0.0.1 [client] socket=/var/lib/mysql/mysql.sock A TCP loopback bind does not configure every additional listener (for example X Protocol); inventory those separately. Add the narrow approved bind address, firewall and TLS requirements before remote use. Verify mounts and existing data before starting; an empty wrong path can be initialized as a new instance by package helpers.

title: Every source option, interpreted for 8.4
context: Databases · Get a server running · MySQL · Configuration and systemd services
text: Source option/group Review and replacement guidance innodb_buffer_pool_size=5600M; 70%/10% comments Not a portable default. Measure memory limits/working set, connection buffers, other services and OS headroom; 128 MiB is the ordinary small default unless other sizing automation changes it. disable_log_bin Disables binary logging and breaks ordinary binlog replication/PITR. Only choose deliberately for a role that does not need it; never a routine performance fix. binlog_expire_logs_seconds=604800 Seven-day example, not a safe universal retention window. Keep all logs required by backups, delayed/disconnected replicas and recovery policy. Historical expire_logs_days is not the 8.4 configuration to revive. binlog_encryption=ON Requires supported initialized key management; verify binlog/relay-log encryption, key backups and remote recovery access. Does not encrypt every database/log file. binlog_do_db=test Source-side filtering can omit required changes with format-dependent semantics. Avoid casual filtering on a source used for full recovery. slow_query_log, slow_query_log_file, long_query_time=10 Enable with explicit file/output, threshold and retention; ten seconds is an example/default, not a tuning recommendation. general_log, general_log_file=general.index General logging can capture secrets/PII and add load. The .index suffix does not make it a binary-log index. Use descriptive paths and restrict access. join_buffer_size=128M, sort_buffer_size=2M, read_rnd_buffer_size=2M Connection/operation memory can multiply across concurrency. Do not allocate globally on a “reporting servers are different” slogan; measure queries and session-scope changes where appropriate. default-authentication-plugin=mysql_native_password Removed default_authentication_plugin configuration is invalid in 8.4. mysql_native_password is disabled by default; upgrade clients for caching_sha2_password and TLS rather than weakening auth globally. plugin_load_add=group_replication.so, mysql_clone.so Distinct optional plugins; clone has overwrite/compatibility prerequisites. group_replication_communication_stack, group UUID, local address, seeds Must match a designed compatible topology and secure communication; copied UUIDs/two-host examples do not establish quorum or HA. Single-/multi-primary settings Do not switch off single-primary or enable update-everywhere checks without reviewing Group Replication restrictions and application conflict handling. server_id Unique nonzero replication identity; not enough by itself because server UUIDs must be unique too. gtid_mode=ON, enforce_gtid_consistency=ON Suitable planned new-topology settings; existing OFF topologies require the coordinated transition sequence. port=3307, multiple bind_address values Resolve listener conflicts, supported syntax, firewall/SELinux and client routing. Neither setting assigns resource isolation or secures all listeners. datadir, socket, log-error, pid-file Paths must match service layout/permissions/labels and be unique per instance. /var/run is commonly /run; runtime directories must be created by the appropriate service/package mechanism. lc_messages_dir Must refer to message files from the selected distribution; tarball paths do not necessarily match RPM layout. log_timestamps=SYSTEM Chooses local time for supported logs; UTC is often easier for distributed correlation. Record timezone/DST assumptions if using SYSTEM. user=mysql OS process identity, not a SQL user; use the installed service account. [mysqld1] Used by explicit suffix 1; RPM template units use groups like [mysqld@replica01] instead. [mysql] socket mysql client-specific default; [client] applies to supported client programs. Socket values do not automatically select every named instance. Back up current option files, review precedence/includes/persisted settings, validate syntax with the chosen server binary, restart only in the planned window and verify effective variables/listeners/logs. To roll back, restore the reviewed prior settings; do not assume deleting an option undoes a persisted value. [17][19][20][21][46][47][58][67][69][86][90]

title: Prefer the vendor unit
context: Databases · Get a server running · MySQL · Configuration and systemd services
text: Target: RHEL 9 x86-64 Oracle MySQL 8.4 RPM installation. Read systemctl cat mysqld.service and existing drop-ins. Use the installed package’s unit, not the historical complete replacement below. Generic archives may lack its paths, helper and systemd-notification support.

title: Correct the concrete unit defects
context: Databases · Get a server running · MySQL · Configuration and systemd services
text: Source directive Meaning / decision Copyright/header Oracle copyright is retained verbatim. The prose says “forking” but Type=notify describes a notifying service, not Type=forking. After / Wants=network-online.target Ordering and weak dependency; they do not prove DNS/remote storage/application readiness. After=syslog.target Historical ordering choice; retain the vendor’s tested dependencies rather than assuming this controls modern journald. WantedBy=multi-user.target Installation enablement target; enable is distinct from start. User=mysql, Group=mysql Service OS identity; filesystem/policy access must permit all configured paths. Type=notify Works only when the installed server supports and sends readiness notification. Do not silently replace with forking to hide a timeout. TimeoutSec=0 Disables timeout; inherited package behavior is not an argument to remove all operational startup monitoring. PermissionsStartOnly=true Legacy/deprecated systemd control that exempts pre/post commands from some identity settings. Do not copy it into new units as a current best practice; package/version semantics matter. ExecStartPre=/usr/bin/mysqld_pre_systemd RPM helper, not universally shipped. Can initialize an empty datadir; verify required mounts/data before start. ExecStart=/usr/sbin/mysqld $MYSQLD_OPTS Path and option ordering must match package/server behavior. Do not replace with a tarball path without reviewing the entire unit. EnvironmentFile="MYSQLD_OPTS=--defaults-file=/etc/my.cnf" Invalid use: EnvironmentFile takes file paths, not an assignment. Use an actual environment-file path or Environment="MYSQLD_OPTS=..." in a reviewed override. /etc/my.cnf is already a normal RPM option-file location. EnvironmentFile=-/etc/sysconfig/mysql Reads optional assignments from that file; leading - allows missing file. This is not the same as [mysqld] syntax. LimitNOFILE=10000 OS descriptor limit, not a universal workload tuning value; compare effective systemd/server limits. Restart=on-failure, RestartPreventExitStatus=1 Restart policy; repeated failure needs diagnosis, not an endless reset/restart loop. Environment=MYSQLD_PARENT_PID=1 Package integration setting used for restart behavior; not a generic daemonization technique. PrivateTmp=false Does not isolate the service’s temporary namespace. Change hardening options only after verifying file/path and server-feature requirements.

title: A narrow drop-in, not a replacement unit
context: Databases · Get a server running · MySQL · Configuration and systemd services
text: For a validated workload that needs a chosen descriptor ceiling, use systemctl edit mysqld.service and a reviewed fragment such as: [Service] LimitNOFILE=10000 The number is an example decision to verify, not a performance promise. After a unit change, systemctl daemon-reload; schedule a controlled restart, inspect status/error logs and systemctl show mysqld.service -p LimitNOFILE, and verify SQL-level effective limits. mysqld --validate-config does not validate a systemd unit. A unit can also be checked with the installed systemd-analyze verify using the actual unit path, without claiming that static checks prove startup. Rollback only the drop-in you added and reload definitions; do not delete unrelated overrides. Preserve the prior datadir/configuration and verify normal restart. [19][20][105]

title: Connections and query execution
context: Databases · Understand the moving parts · MySQL
text: Logical architecture diagram — external reference. Reuse rights are unresolved; the explanation below does not depend on the image.MySQL 8.4 · connection / requestOne connection, many requestsEstablish the sessionClient ↔ serverAn application connector, mysql CLI or Workbench speaks the MySQL protocol. TCP and local transports are alternatives.Negotiate & authenticateClassic TCP with TLS: server greeting → client SSLRequest → TLS handshake → authentication exchange. Verify the server identity; encryption alone is not identity verification.Connected sessionThe default model uses a server thread per connection, possibly reusing a cached thread. It is not a separate mysqld process.For a SQL requestParse & resolveCheck SQL grammar and resolve referenced objects. Privilege checks apply to the requested operations, not just to login.Choose a planThe optimizer uses statistics and cost estimates to compare the plans it explores. An estimate is not measured runtime.Execute ↔ storage engineThe executor requests rows through the engine interface. InnoDB uses cached pages or storage; results or errors return to the client.Not a literal call stack. Authentication exchanges vary by plugin. Authorization is not a single pre-parse gate. Enterprise Thread Pool changes scheduling; MySQL 8.4 has no server query cache.Teaching simplification of the classic-protocol connection and SQL request paths, not an exact engine schematic. A session can issue many statements; successful login does not authorize every operation.Read the sources Connection protocol [103] · TLS identity [70] · Request privileges [148] · Optimizer limits [139] · Buffer pool [7] · Enterprise features [84] · Removed features [86]External reference, not republished: Earlier logical-architecture image Connectors implement the MySQL protocol for applications. mysql is a command-line client; Workbench is a separate GUI and does not require the mysql CLI to establish every connection. [2][103] Startup: initialize the server and load privilege information; startup is not a user-issued FLUSH PRIVILEGES operation. Connection: clients can use TCP or a local transport such as a Unix socket. For classic-protocol TCP, the server greeting advertises capabilities and authentication information. A TLS-capable client sends SSLRequest, negotiates TLS, then sends authentication data inside that transport. TLS stage What to check ClientHello Client advertises supported protocol versions and cryptographic parameters. Server negotiation Server selects compatible parameters and proves its identity with its certificate and handshake authentication. Exact message ordering differs between TLS 1.2 and 1.3. Certificate validation VERIFY_CA checks the trusted issuer; VERIFY_IDENTITY also checks the requested hostname against the certificate. Merely encrypting a connection does not verify the server. Key agreement Modern TLS uses negotiated key agreement; do not teach RSA-encrypted premaster-secret exchange as the universal handshake. TLS 1.3 does not use that legacy RSA key exchange. Finished messages Authenticate the handshake and establish traffic keys; application data is encrypted and integrity protected. Client certificate Optional unless the account/policy requires it; distinct from password authentication. Authentication: the handshake response identifies the user and client capabilities. The server matches an account including its Host portion, chooses the account’s authentication plugin, and may continue or switch the plugin exchange. The response is plugin-dependent, not universally a password hash. Success yields OK; failure yields ERR. caching_sha2_password is the normal 8.4 choice; update old clients rather than re-enabling legacy authentication by default. [2][3][70][103] 4. Connection manager: the default one-thread-per-connection model can reuse a cached thread or create one. Enterprise Thread Pool changes scheduling; neither model makes a client connection a separate mysqld process. [84] 5. Authorization: the server checks the account’s privileges for requested operations; a successful login does not authorize every query. 6. Parsing: SQL text is tokenized and checked against the grammar, producing internal query structures. This is a conceptual pipeline, not a claim that every AST node is itself a SQL operation or that privilege checking occurs only once before parsing. [148][32] 7. Optimization: the optimizer considers applicable access paths and transformations, index use, join ordering and supported join methods such as nested-loop/hash joins. Statistics and cardinality estimates feed cost estimates; they are not measured runtime. It chooses among the plans it explores, not an exhaustive guaranteed global optimum. The InnoDB adaptive hash index is an internal engine optimization, not a named SQL index hint. Use EXPLAIN and, for a safe bounded query, EXPLAIN ANALYZE to compare estimates with execution; the latter executes the query. [32][34][9][139] 8. Execution and storage engines: the executor requests rows through the engine interface. InnoDB reads cached pages or fetches them from storage. Changes dirty buffer-pool pages and generate redo; commit durability and later page flushing are different events. Cache Meaning Table open cache Reuses open table objects; file-descriptor consumption depends on engine and configuration. Data dictionary object cache Reuses metadata; distinguish it from InnoDB’s buffer pool. Historical query cache Deprecated in 5.7.20 and removed in 8.0. No MySQL 8.4 server query cache setting exists. Application caching requires explicit invalidation and consistency decisions. Key cache Caches MyISAM index blocks, not InnoDB rows. InnoDB buffer pool Caches index and data pages, including clean and dirty pages. [4][7][86]

title: Group replication and failover
context: Databases · Keep more than one copy · MySQL
text: Group Replication orders/certifies transactions and manages membership; it is not “every replica synchronously applies every commit.” Remote apply can lag. Choose group_replication_consistency behavior for read-after-write/failover needs; in 8.4 its default is BEFORE_ON_PRIMARY_FAILOVER, not a universal linearizable-read guarantee. Single-primary normally routes writes to one member; multi-primary has additional workload restrictions and certification conflicts. title: TLS and encryption at rest
context: Databases · Protect it and change it safely · MySQL
text: TLS protects connections; InnoDB encryption protects selected stored data when the corresponding keys are available. Neither replaces least privilege, host security, patching, backups or audit/restore tests. Server, replication, administrative and client connections may use different TLS settings. TLS certificate and transport procedure: trust/hostname verification, separate key permissions, planned rotation and rollback. The old SSL.sh is retained there only as historical text, with the world-readable-key bug explained. Keyring and encryption procedure: component availability, early loading, key custody, explicitly enabled data/log encryption and restore testing. The old TDE.sh only attempted to load an Enterprise encrypted-file keyring; it did not implement complete TDE. For 8.4 Community, evaluate component_keyring_file with its documented threat model; the encrypted-file keyring component is Enterprise. Local file keyrings are not, by themselves, a regulatory-compliance key-management solution. Backup keys separately and verify recovery on an isolated server before claiming data is recoverable. [67][68][69][70][93] Historical source example for reading, not a tested procedure or executable download. Applies to MySQL Server 8.4 LTS; the production baseline is RHEL 9 x86_64 with Oracle MySQL Community RPMs from the MySQL Yum repository. Separately licensed products and other platforms are identified explicitly.[1][72] Target: MySQL 8.4 LTS on the selected EL9 RPM platform; use the distribution’s supported OpenSSL build and your organization’s CA/PKI workflow. The OpenSSL 3.x reference explains request/SAN syntax, but no versionless certificate-generation script is recommended. The historical source is reproduced below as text only; do not execute it. Inventory every endpoint/client (classic, X Protocol, admin interface and replication separately), DNS names/IPs actually used, current account TLS requirements, CA trust, protocol/cipher policy and expiry/rotation policy. Back up current config/certificates securely, keep an authenticated administrative connection and console/rollback access, and rehearse on an isolated instance. Have the CA issue the server certificate for its real identity with appropriate DNS/IP subjectAltName entries and key usage. A certificate for an IP will not automatically verify an unrelated DNS hostname. Modern CA policy, not the source’s fixed ten-year validity or empty APP_NAME/IP, determines lifetime. The CA private key belongs in protected CA custody, not the MySQL datadir. Generate/store server and optional client private keys separately; do not deploy every .pem produced in a working directory. Validate chain, identity, expiry and certificate/key match using the CA’s tooling and the selected OpenSSL documentation before modifying the server. For REQUIRE X509 or subject/issuer-constrained accounts, each client additionally needs its own suitable certificate and private key. REQUIRE SSL alone requires encrypted transport, not necessarily a client certificate. After installing explicitly selected files into the approved server-readable directory, set permissions by role: File Example EL9 ownership/mode Custody server-key.pem mysql:mysql, 0600 (or a narrowly scoped equivalent needed by the service) Server private key; never world-readable. server-cert.pem root-owned, 0644 with service read access Public certificate; integrity still matters. ca.pem root-owned, 0644 with service read access Public trust chain, not the CA signing key. Client private key Owned by the specific client OS identity, 0600 On the client host; not shared among replicas by default. CA private key Not installed on the DB server Protected CA system/backup with separate access control. Ensure parent directories and SELinux labels permit the intended reads. Use exact paths, not chmod 644 *.pem: that wildcard overwrites restrictive key modes and was the source’s blocking defect. Check ACLs as well as numeric mode. If that script was ever used operationally, treat exposed private keys as potentially compromised and plan revocation/reissue rather than merely changing mode afterward. Edit the correct existing [mysqld] group in a reviewed option-file copy. [server] is also a server-read group, but the old script only searched for that heading and missed the supplied file’s [mysqld]. Do not delete every matching TLS line across all groups or duplicate contradictory settings. [mysqld] ssl_ca=/var/lib/mysql/tls/ca.pem ssl_cert=/var/lib/mysql/tls/server-cert.pem ssl_key=/var/lib/mysql/tls/server-key.pem require_secure_transport=ON These are example approved file locations to provision/label first. Check permitted local transports and all legacy clients before enforcing require_secure_transport. This setting by itself does not force every client to authenticate the server identity. Do not pin one TLS 1.3 ciphersuite from a copied script without validating client compatibility and organizational policy; TLS 1.2/1.3 cipher settings differ. A classic-protocol client verification example, with actual host/account/CA inputs: mysql --host=db.example.com --user=operator --password \ --ssl-mode=VERIFY_IDENTITY --ssl-ca=/etc/mysql/trust/ca.pem Within that session, inspect SHOW SESSION STATUS LIKE 'Ssl_cipher'; and Ssl_version; empty cipher indicates no TLS for that session. A cipher alone does not prove hostname verification: deliberately test that an untrusted CA/wrong hostname is rejected in a controlled test. Inspect server startup/TLS diagnostics and account requirements, and test application plus replication clients before accepting the change. Place validated cert/key files in their final paths before a restart/reload. Avoid stopping first then using mv *.pem from an arbitrary current directory. Use a deliberate maintenance restart for initial setup; for rotation, the documented ALTER INSTANCE RELOAD TLS interface can update supported server TLS contexts without restarting, with version/channel behavior checked first. Existing connections may retain their old TLS sessions; test new connections. Retain previous usable certificate/configuration until validation is complete, subject to revocation/security rules. On failure, restore only the known prior files/settings and reload/restart the intended context; do not disable verification globally or expose plaintext just to get an application online. Rotate client trust in a staged overlap window where needed, monitor expiry and test backup/recovery of required keys. Never keep an exposed/revoked key solely as a convenient rollback. The server example uses /var/lib/mysql/tls, inside the standard data tree, so its server-read files can use the existing mysqld_db_t data-tree policy instead of leaving a novel /etc/mysql/tls path unprovisioned. Provision it as a restricted directory (for example root-owned, group mysql, mode 0750); deploy only the selected server key, server certificate and public CA chain with the file-specific permissions above. Apply restorecon -Rv /var/lib/mysql/tls and inspect ls -ldZ / ls -lZ before starting. Confirm effective policy on this installed RHEL system; for a relocated datadir use its equivalence mapping and update the TLS paths deliberately. Replication-side SOURCE_SSL_CA, SOURCE_SSL_CERT and SOURCE_SSL_KEY are read by mysqld on the replica; provision and label them there too. Ordinary client’s --ssl-ca is read by the client OS identity and is a separate path/access contract. The CA private key is never copied into either directory. Do not solve a certificate/key read denial by giving all users read permission. Keep a backup exclusion/inclusion inventory: a physical datadir copy may now include these private keys, so encrypt/restrict that backup and retain controlled recovery access. Keep a backup exclusion/inclusion inventory: a physical datadir copy may now include these private keys, so encrypt/restrict that backup and retain controlled recovery access. title: A keyring is not complete transparent data encryption
context: Databases · Protect it and change it safely · MySQL · TLS and encryption at rest
text: Target: MySQL 8.4 LTS. The source names component_keyring_encrypted_file, an Enterprise Edition component, not a universally available Community plugin. Community has component_keyring_file; external key-management implementations have separate platform/edition/service dependencies. Both local file-based components have limited threat models and are not stand-alone regulatory-compliance solutions. Do not run the historical script below. It stops a service, overwrites hardcoded files, embeds a configuration password and omits key recovery, permissions and encryption enablement. No literal credential survives in the preserved snapshot.

title: Select and establish the keyring
context: Databases · Protect it and change it safely · MySQL · TLS and encryption at rest
text: Inventory existing encrypted tablespaces/logs and the already active keyring. Never replace/reinitialize a keyring that holds keys needed by existing data. Confirm edition, selected component library, exact server/plugin paths and backup-tool compatibility. Read the component’s version-specific manifest/configuration rules. A global mysqld.my belongs alongside the actual mysqld executable; local manifests may be read from the instance datadir when enabled. The source’s /sbin/mysqld.my and /lib64/mysql/plugin/... are not portable paths. Components needed to open encrypted InnoDB data must load early through the documented manifest mechanism, not a late generic plugin recipe. Preserve existing manifest entries rather than overwriting the file. Determine whether global versus local component configuration is appropriate for multiple instances. Each instance needs independent custody/access to the intended key store, not an accidental shared keyring path. For the encrypted-file component, provision path, the configuration password, and read_only as documented. Supply the secret through a controlled secret-management/deployment process; it is not safe simply because it sits inside JSON. Restrict the config and keyring files/directories to required OS identities, apply ownership/SELinux policy and ensure the keyring path is not publicly readable or casually backed up with its unlocking secret beside it. Start/restart only in a maintenance window after a tested rollback/backup plan. Inspect server errors and performance_schema.keyring_component_status; verify the selected component/path/status. A returned status row proves neither that all tables are encrypted nor that backup recovery works.

title: Explicitly enable and verify each encryption scope
context: Databases · Protect it and change it safely · MySQL · TLS and encryption at rest
text: Scope Action/check New InnoDB file-per-table/general tablespaces Review supported ENCRYPTION='Y' DDL and default_table_encryption / privilege controls. Defaults govern creation and do not retroactively encrypt every old table. Existing tables For a compatible file-per-table table, ALTER TABLE app.table_name ENCRYPTION='Y'; is a deliberate storage operation with time/space/lock implications. Shared/general tablespace encryption is changed at its appropriate tablespace scope, not with an arbitrary per-table operation. Back up and rehearse first. mysql system tablespace Separate supported system-tablespace encryption control/DDL; not covered merely by setting an application schema default. Redo / undo Review and explicitly enable innodb_redo_log_encrypt / innodb_undo_log_encrypt where required, with recovery/keyring prerequisites. Observe transition behavior; do not infer all preexisting bytes change instantly. Binary / relay logs binlog_encryption is a separate feature. Retain keys and use the supported server-mediated reading/recovery path for encrypted logs. Temporary storage, general/slow/error/audit logs, exports Not automatically protected by the above table settings. Evaluate each documented coverage boundary and disk/log/backup encryption separately. Backups Database encryption and backup-image encryption differ. Confirm the backup product can capture/restore encrypted tables and key material for this exact component/version. Inspect the relevant Information Schema InnoDB tablespace encryption metadata and actual configuration after each change. Test reads/writes and restart. Do not declare “TDE complete” because only the component was loaded or a default changed.

title: Key lifecycle, restore and rollback
context: Databases · Protect it and change it safely · MySQL · TLS and encryption at rest
text: Back up the data and every key/keyring state needed by that backup under separate access controls, including component configuration and the securely recoverable unlocking secret. Document who can recover them during a host/CA/KMS outage; encrypt/protect backups off-host and retain key history as long as dependent data/log backups exist. ALTER INSTANCE ROTATE INNODB MASTER KEY rotates the InnoDB master key under its documented privileges and prerequisites; it is not a rotation of every unrelated log/audit/backup encryption key. Test rotation, keyring backup update, restart and reading older retained backups. Do not delete an old key because a new key was created. The acceptance test is an isolated restore to compatible binaries/component configuration using only the retained backup and recovery key material: start, read encrypted objects, validate application data and replay the required logs. Also test the expected controlled failure when keys are unavailable, without damaging the only copies. Rollback is not unloading/removing the keyring while data still needs it. Keep the working component/keyring available; reverse a failed configuration deployment only to a configuration that can still read the required keys. If changing encryption policy, use supported decrypt/reencrypt/migration steps with backups and revalidation. Lose the necessary keys and the encrypted data may be unrecoverable.

title: Community file keyring on the selected RHEL host
context: Databases · Protect it and change it safely · MySQL · TLS and encryption at rest
text: For a new, single instance with no existing keyring or encrypted data, Community’s component_keyring_file is a concrete alternative to the historical Enterprise-only encrypted-file script. First inspect @@plugin_dir, the actual RPM mysqld executable path and all existing manifests. Only one keyring implementation may be enabled; changing one for existing encrypted data requires a supported key migration, not the following new-instance setup. For the selected /usr/sbin/mysqld, the global manifest is /usr/sbin/mysqld.my: {"components":"file://component_keyring_file"} Place component_keyring_file.cnf beside its actual component library in the queried plugin directory, not an assumed /lib64 path: {"path":"/var/lib/mysql-keyring/component_keyring_file.keys","read_only":false} The keyring data path must not point into the MySQL datadir. Provision the approved /var/lib/mysql-keyring independently of /var/lib/mysql, owned by the service identity with mode 0700 and no unnecessary ACL access. Keep manifest/configuration root-controlled and server-readable but not server-writable (for example root:mysql 0640, with traversable parent directories); restrict key data to the required service identity. The component’s local key file is not encrypted merely because its filename contains “keyring”. Inspect the installed policy and expected labels first. For this mutable MySQL-owned key data directory, a reviewed mysqld_db_t file-context mapping plus restorecon is the data-access policy pattern; do not label the manifest, component library and all configuration as writable database data. Verify actual process/file contexts and any AVC during the controlled restart. If policy denies access, diagnose the specific path/type/permission rather than widening all file modes or disabling enforcement. With multiple instances sharing the executable/plugin directory, do not deploy the preceding global-only key-path configuration: it would make them share one key file. Use the documented global read_local_manifest:true and read_local_config:true routing, place each local manifest/configuration in its corresponding datadir, and select a distinct external key-store path per instance. Provision and test every instance affected by the shared global files before restarting any of them. Retain the original working files for rollback. After the planned restart, inspect SELECT * FROM performance_schema.keyring_component_status;, error logs and the actual key-store permissions/labels; Active means component initialization, not encrypted tables or recoverable backups. Explicitly enable only the intended encryption scopes described above. A backup of the datadir alone omits this external key directory: include its version-consistent key material, manifests/configuration and recovery access in a separately protected backup set and prove an isolated encrypted-data restore before relying on the configuration. [46][67][68][69][93][167][106][157][115]
